tools.name: Naive Agents + Sessions + Events (core runtime)
tools.what_it_is: Hosted managed-agent runtime (formerly 'vetta'). An Agent is a versioned config (model, harness, system prompt, tools, mcp_servers, skills, multiagent roster, handoffs, budget, notifications, output_schema). A Session is a durable, resumable run of an agent; Events are a seq-ordered, resumable log/SSE stream.
key_capabilities: Sessions can run for hours and sit idle for days at storage cost only; idle != done, branch on stop_reason
Send input to an idle session to resume it: POST /v1/sessions/{id}/messages (message, interrupt, queue, model, mode plan|build)
stop_reasons: end_turn, awaiting_input, awaiting_approval, awaiting_answer, awaiting_delegation, budget_paused, interrupted, max_iterations, error, context_exhausted
Resumable SSE via client.stream(sessionId,{afterSeq}) or paged GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events
Per-session overrides: window, budget_micro_usd, identity, output_schema, structured_output_required, metadata, mode
Plan mode (read-only planning, person must approve the plan)
Harnesses: pi (default, micro-VM), vetta (preview), claude_code, hermes
Agent workspace/computer persists across that agent's sessions (same files)
tools.api_and_setup: npm i @usenaive-sdk/managed-agents (ESM-only, TS only, zod dependency; no Python SDK). createClient({ baseUrl: 'https://api.vetta.sh', apiKey: process.env.NAIVE_API_KEY }). CLI: npm i -g @usenaive-sdk/cli (`naive`). REST base https://api.vetta.sh/v1, Bearer sk_live_ org-scoped keys with scopes, Vetta-Version header (current 2026-09-30), Idempotency-Key on writes. GET /v1/openapi.json (no key) lists 410 live routes. A paid plan is required for every non-billing route (402 subscription_required): Standard $20/mo incl. $20 credit, 7-day trial with $10 credit (card required); Pro $200/mo. Rate limits: 6000 req/min/org, 3000 req/min/key, 50 concurrently running sessions (extra queue). Computer: $0.0666/hr per running 1vCPU/1GiB session box, $0 while paused.
tools.role_in_product: Every procurement worker (scout, outreach, negotiator, logistics, founder-liaison) is a Naive agent; each supplier conversation can be one long-lived session that parks while waiting for a reply and is resumed by our relay when the supplier answers.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: The Shenzhen time-zone trick fits the runtime: outreach session goes idle Saturday evening SF, costs ~nothing overnight, and our WeChat/email relay wakes the exact negotiation session with POST /v1/sessions/{id}/messages when a reply lands.

tools.name: Naive Human-in-the-loop (ask_operator, ask policies, approvals, notifications)
tools.what_it_is: Built-in pause/resume primitives: the ask_operator tool parks a session with a structured question (1-3 fields); any tool set to permission 'ask' parks on awaiting_approval; agent-level email notifications deep-link the founder to the parked session.
key_capabilities: ask_operator: session goes idle with stop_reason awaiting_answer and a pending_actions row kind 'question' with prompt + fields (text, choice with options/other, multiple, optional; 2026-09-30 adds connect and media fields)
Answer via POST /v1/sessions/{id}/answers {tool_call_id, answers:{key:value}} → session resumes automatically; the answer folds into the next turn as the tool result
Tool policies allow|ask|deny per tool; confirm via POST /v1/sessions/{id}/tool_confirmations (allow/deny + reason); approver principal is audited
Agent `notifications` {email, approvals, questions, updates} emails the founder with a deep link to the paused session; on a team, members' questions route to the coordinator's session
GET /v1/digest lists every session waiting on a person (awaiting_approval / awaiting_answer / budget_paused); CLI `naive session inbox` and `naive session answer`
A held tool or question burns no budget while waiting
Many outbound tools ask by default: email.send, phone.send, card.issue, wallet.pay, mobile, data_run, etc.
Deployments skip the next cron fire while a run is waiting on you
tools.api_and_setup: Enable ask_operator (on by default; set permission 'deny' to disable). Requires a harness with the approvals capability (pi yes; claude_code/hermes no: a session whose toolset has an 'ask' is refused at start on those). SDK: naive.sessions.answer(id,{tool_call_id, answers}), naive.sessions.confirmTool(id,{tool_call_id, decision}). Subscribe a webhook to session.idle and branch on stop_reason + pending_actions[].kind.
tools.role_in_product: Step 4/5 of the product: the coordinator writes the decision memo, then calls ask_operator('Proceed with Supplier X at $Y/unit, MOQ Z?', fields: decision choice [proceed, counter, reject], note). The founder answers from the email link, Studio, or our own SMS/Slack relay that calls /answers; the session resumes and executes next steps.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: Gate first-contact WeChat/email sends and any commitment (sample payment, PO) with 'ask', while follow-ups inside hard limits run on 'allow'. The founder's 'proceed' resumes the exact session that then messages the supplier on WeChat to arrange samples and shipping.

tools.name: Naive Custom Tools via MCP servers (incl. Naive's own MCP and app MCP endpoints)
tools.what_it_is: The way to give agents our own tools today. Agents declare up to 20 remote MCP servers (public HTTPS URLs); tools appear as <server>.<tool> and are gated by the same allow/ask/deny policy. Client-executed JSON-schema 'custom tools' are documented as COMING SOON.
key_capabilities: mcp_servers: [{type:'url', name, url}] on the agent; tools configured in tools.configs keyed 'server.tool'
Default permission for MCP tools is 'ask'; must explicitly 'allow' per tool (no server-wide trust)
Auth injected server-side from the vault (static_bearer or mcp_oauth) matched by URL; secret-bearing inline headers rejected; sandbox/model never see the token
≤100 tools per server; schemas/responses capped; failures surface as session.degraded and retry next wake
A Naive-hosted fullstack app can expose an MCP path ('mcp': '/mcp'); every agent with access gets its tools as <app>.<tool>, with auto-minted VETTA_MCP_TOKEN
POST /v1/mcp exposes the Naive API itself as an MCP catalog (agents_create, sessions_*…), admin scope needed to declare it on an agent
MCP sessions: short-lived, revocable, tool-allowlisted bearers
tools.api_and_setup: Host an MCP server (Streamable HTTP JSON-RPC) on Vercel or Render at a public https URL; create a vault credential kind static_bearer for that URL (POST /v1/vaults, /v1/vaults/{id}/credentials); add mcp_servers + tools.configs on the agent. Localhost/private IPs are refused (400 validation_failed). env_var vault credentials are not available (501).
tools.role_in_product: Our integration bus. Build one 'procurement-ops' MCP server exposing: wechat.send / wechat.read_thread (bridge to a Mobilerun phone running WeChat), alibaba.search (Apify actor), supplier.lookup (Monid tools), agentmail.send/read, crm.upsert (HubSpot), stripe.create_payment_link, ledger.record_offer (Neon). tools.role_in_supplier_route: This is how the WeChat route plugs into Naive: wechat.send/read as MCP tools backed by Mobilerun (the sponsor's real phones) so the agent never needs to drive the phone pixel-by-pixel itself; replies captured by the bridge are pushed back into the right session via the Naive REST API.

tools.what_it_is: A team is an agent with a `multiagent` roster (type coordinator, 1-20 members by id@version, 'self', or an 'advisor' model). Coordination is via send_to_agent delegation (wait:true, one level deep) and a durable shared board of cards that outlive sessions.

key_findings: Custom tools: the only way to add our own tools today is remote MCP servers. You can declare up to 20 public HTTPS servers per agent (≤100 tools each), with auth injected from the vault (static_bearer or mcp_oauth). A Naive-hosted fullstack app with an `mcp` path also works. Client-executed JSON-schema 'custom tools' are marked COMING SOON, and localhost URLs are refused. So host a `procurement-ops` MCP server on Vercel or Render. It wraps WeChat (through Mobilerun), Apify, Monid, AgentMail, HubSpot, Stripe and Neon, and enforces the hard negotiation limits server-side. Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/tools.md

Human-in-the-loop DOES exist, contrary to the earlier assumption. The `ask_operator` tool parks a session (idle, stop_reason awaiting_answer) with a structured question. POST /v1/sessions/{id}/answers resumes it automatically. Any tool set to permission `ask` parks on awaiting_approval and is resolved through POST /v1/sessions/{id}/tool_confirmations. Agent `notifications.email` emails the founder a deep link for approvals and questions. GET /v1/digest and `naive session inbox` list everything waiting on a person. Waiting costs no budget. This requires the pi harness, since claude_code and hermes cannot hold approvals. Sources: https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/session-operations.md, https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/agents.md

Resume model: any idle session resumes when you POST /v1/sessions/{id}/messages. There is NO generic inbound webhook that resumes a session. Inbound email or SMS to an identity's inbox or number starts a NEW session of the owning agent rather than continuing the old one, and it is rate-guarded (5/hr per sender, 20/hr per inbox, 10 thread turns/day). So run a small relay (Render/Vercel + Neon) that maps supplier thread → session_id or board card. On each WeChat/email reply it calls sessions.send on the negotiation session, or PATCHes the supplier's board card back to todo, which wakes the assignee. Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/identity/inbound.md

Identity gives each persona a real email inbox on a free one-call system domain, with inbound wake and $0.0008 per send; email.send asks by default. It also gives US phone numbers with INBOUND SMS only: outbound SMS returns 501 feature_not_configured, and an org can hold at most 3 numbers. There is no telephony voice: Naive 'voice calls' are in-app user↔agent calls at $0.08/min with a 10-minute cap. A voice call to a supplier would need another provider. Sources: https://usenaive.ai/docs/identity/email.md, https://usenaive.ai/docs/identity/phone.md, https://usenaive.ai/docs/platform/pricing.md

Alibaba login persistence: yes, via saved-login contexts. Set context_name with persist_context, or use human_login so the founder signs in once in live view and clears Alibaba's slider/SMS check. Credentials can also go in the vault as login:<service>. Reusing a saved login needs an explicit dashboard grant per agent or role. Run the browser with region ap-southeast, stealth, a residential proxy (needs scoped allowed_domains) and allow_writes so it can send messages. GOTCHA: on saved-login sessions, extract/observe/screenshot redact email and phone patterns, which may hide supplier contact details. The agent's browser also closes whenever the session parks. Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/computer/browser.md

WeChat route recommendation: do NOT rely on Naive's own mobile sandbox for WeChat. Its devices are disposable (no pause or persistence), the agent tool is capped at 60 min, WeChat availability in the app catalogue is unconfirmed, and WeChat allows only one active phone login. Use a persistent Mobilerun device (the Best Mobile Automation track requires Mobilerun anyway) with WeChat logged in once. Expose it to Naive as MCP tools: wechat.send(contact, text), wechat.read_new(), wechat.add_contact(wechat_id, greeting). A bridge process polls new messages and pushes them into the right Naive session. Naive mobile (Singapore 'as' jurisdiction, $0.05/min Android) is the fallback. Sources: https://usenaive.ai/docs/computer/mobile.md, https://mobilerun.ai/blog/posts/autonomous-company-hackathon-naive-mobilerun

Teams: an agent with `multiagent` {type:'coordinator', agents:[1-20 id@version | self | advisor]}. There are two mechanisms. send_to_agent(wait:true) is one-level delegation, folded back into the coordinator's turn. The durable shared board has cards (todo/doing/blocked/done, assignee, blocked_by); assigning a card wakes the assignee in its own session, the board ticks every minute, and the coordinator gets a digest session when cards reach done or blocked. Routes /v1/boards/* are live in openapi.json. CAVEAT: skill.md still lists 'multiagent teams' as coming soon, so verify with a live key at kickoff. Sources: https://usenaive.ai/docs/team/overview.md, https://usenaive.ai/docs/team/board.md, https://usenaive.ai/skill.md

Autonomy trap to test in hour 1: once a chat has 'read people's data' (contacts, mail, messages, a connected app), several things change even at `allow`. Every send, board_write, mobile, web_fetch and every MCP or connected-app tool asks a human each time, and bash is refused. Supplier replies should therefore arrive as plain session input from our relay, not through platform mail reads, if we want unattended negotiation. Whether the inbound wake or relay input triggers this flag is not documented. Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/tools.md

Models: a live catalogue of 'hundreds' of tool-calling models (GET /v1/models, needs a key). Docs examples are z-ai/glm-5.3-flash (default in examples), deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731, zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 and vetta/auto. Completion windows are immediate / priority / loose, with loose cheapest for overnight Shenzhen work but only on window-supported models. Anthropic- and OpenAI-format proxy endpoints are available. Standard is $20/mo with $20 credit, plus a 7-day trial with $10 credit that needs a card; Pro is $200/mo. RECOMMENDED ARCHITECTURE. All agents on the pi harness with budgets, under one company/org. (1) 'Head of Procurement' coordinator: strong model, immediate window, notifications.email = founder. It owns the board, writes the DecisionMemo (structured output + publish_file) and calls ask_operator {decision: proceed|counter|reject, note}. (2) Scout: web_search/web_fetch, data_run (trade, companies, reviews), browser on alibaba.com/made-in-china.com (ap-southeast, stealth, proxy, saved buyer login), plus Apify via MCP. It outputs SupplierQuote JSON and creates one board card per supplier. (3) Outreach: MCP wechat.* (Mobilerun bridge), Alibaba Messenger through the logged-in browser, and email through a Naive inbox or AgentMail via MCP. First contact is set to `ask` only for the demo's first run, then `allow`. Messages are written in Mandarin. (4) Negotiator: MCP propose_offer/accept_terms, with hard limits (max unit price, MOQ, sample budget) enforced in the MCP server and in Neon. It cannot commit money; Stripe payment links and card tools stay on `ask`. (5) Logistics/Next-steps: after 'proceed' it messages the supplier on WeChat to confirm samples, shipping address and schedule, logs to HubSpot (connection) and creates follow-up cards. Infrastructure: a relay on Render/Vercel + Neon maps wechat_contact/email_thread → {board_card_id, session_id}. It receives Mobilerun bridge events and AgentMail webhooks, then calls POST /v1/sessions/{id}/messages or PATCHes the card. It also receives Naive session.idle webhooks and texts or Slacks the founder when stop_reason = awaiting_answer, translating the reply into POST /v1/sessions/{id}/answers. Deployments: a Saturday 18:00 SF outreach blast, a 30-minute 'loose' overnight follow-up sweep, and a 07:00 SF morning memo. Effort is about 22 to 25 hours across a 3-4 person team.

tools.name: Mobilerun Cloud (REST API + TS/Python SDK + hosted MCP server)
tools.what_it_is: Mobilerun is the renamed DroidRun, made by Droidrun GmbH, with code in the github.com/droidrun org. It is a cloud of Android phones (a virtual 'Android Phone' type plus pooled on-demand Android) and real physical iPhones that LLM agents control. You can send it a natural-language task, which its own mobile agent carries out by reading the accessibility tree or screenshots and then tapping, swiping and typing. You can also call low-level device actions over REST, the SDKs or MCP. Phones are persistent: apps and logins survive between tasks, and a parked device keeps its data without being billed. It also has receive-only SMS numbers, mailboxes for one-time codes, residential proxies, eSIM (Enterprise only), webhooks, scheduled flows and triggers, recordings, and a live WebRTC view.
key_capabilities: Natural-language tasks: POST /v1/tasks {deviceId, task, llmModel, maxSteps, executionTimeout<=2700s, outputSchema (JSON Schema), systemPrompt, apps, credentials, vision, reasoning, humanize, recordingEnabled, vpnCountry}. GET /tasks/{id}/status returns status, succeeded, message, output and steps. GET /tasks/{id}/trajectory returns per-step screenshots and the UI elements the agent touched.

Models for the on-device agent: mobilerun/mobile-agent-fast and mobilerun/mobile-agent-thinking, Claude Opus and Sonnet 4.x, Gemini 3.x, GPT-5.4, GPT-6-luna (the account default), and Kimi K2.6. LLM usage is billed in Mobilerun credits, so no separate model key is needed.

Low-level device API: tap by coordinates, swipe, global actions, keyboard text input (with humanize, wpm and errorRate options), clipboard get and set, deep links, app install, start and stop, permission grant and revoke, file upload and download, screenshots, and GET /devices/{id}/ui-state. ui-state returns an a11y_tree (text, resourceId, contentDescription, bounds) plus phone_state (currentApp, focusedElement).

Hosted MCP server at https://api.mobilerun.ai/v1/mcp. It is stateless Streamable HTTP, authenticated with a Bearer dr_sk_ key, and exposes 39 tools, including run_task, get_task, send_task_message, stop_task, get_task_media, get_device_screenshot, get_device_ui_state, device_action, manage_device_apps, manage_device_files, numbers, mailboxes and webhooks.
Persistence: Android Phones are described as 'dedicated, persistent'. Stopping parks a device: it is not billed and keeps its data, apps and identity. Resume brings it back. Reset wipes it.

Webhooks for task.run.* events, sms.received, mailbox.message.received, chat.input.required and workflow events. Deliveries are signed with HMAC-SHA256, tried 3 times, and dropped after 24 hours. Flows and triggers can run on cron, rrule or one-time schedules, with jitter.
A credentials vault per app package, which can link to 1Password. Secret values are never returned to the agent.
Call media: the browser's microphone and camera can be piped into the device, but only from the Cloud stream view. There is no API for it.
An embeddable device stream lets you show the live phone inside your own dashboard (guide at /guides/embed-device-stream).
Prebuilt app-agent guides exist for Alibaba (Alibaba and 1688 supplier inbox, quote/MOQ/terms extracted as JSON, drafting counter-offers), AliExpress, WhatsApp and Telegram. There is no WeChat guide.

tools.role_in_product: Mobilerun gives the procurement department hands on a phone. Use it for every channel that only exists in a mobile app (WeChat, Alibaba.com app chat, 1688, WhatsApp) or where the app is the trusted surface. The Naive coordinator agent decides what to say within the negotiation limits. Mobilerun carries it out in the app and returns structured JSON: the supplier's reply text, price, MOQ, lead time and certifications. tools.role_in_supplier_route:
Mobilerun is the only practical way into WeChat. Personal WeChat has no send/receive API, and hook or protocol bots get banned.

How the route would work:
1. Keep one persistent phone, logged in to WeChat and the Alibaba.com app.
2. The Naive agent calls run_task with prompts such as "Open WeChat, open the chat with <supplier remark>, send this exact Chinese text: ..." or "Open the WeChat chat list and, for each unread chat, return {contact, last_messages[], timestamps}", with an outputSchema.
3. Because Shenzhen replies arrive while SF sleeps, a scheduled Mobilerun flow or a Naive cron polls overnight. Webhooks (task.run.completed) wake the Naive session.
4. To add a supplier, upload their QR code (from the Alibaba profile or a business card) to the phone's gallery via the files API and use WeChat's Scan, then Album. Or search their WeChat ID or phone number, tap Add to Contacts, and include a verification note.
5. Read Alibaba.com app Messenger threads and extract quotes the same way. Mobilerun's own Alibaba guide demonstrates this.
6. After the founder approves, send the 'proceed' message and ask for a sample proforma invoice (PI) and a shipping schedule.
limitations_risks: WeChat officially lists 'Using an Android emulator ... or non-official plugins to run WeChat' as a reason to block accounts. Mobilerun's docs call the Android Phone a 'virtual Android device' and use the word 'physical' only for iPhones. Running WeChat on a Mobilerun virtual Android is therefore an account-ban risk. Prefer a real iPhone or a connected personal Android phone.

iPhones often have no accessibility tree: ui-state returns 400 DEVICE_TOOL_UNSUPPORTED on devices without accessibility support. WeChat tasks on an iPhone may need vision=true, which costs more and is slower.
A device runs one task at a time. A task waiting for a busy device fails after 30 seconds with 'Device is currently in use'. Send WeChat messages one after another, or use one device per channel.
executionTimeout is capped at 2,700 seconds (45 minutes) and maxSteps defaults to 100, so long inbox sweeps need to be split up.

Voice: there is no API for injecting audio. Call media only works from the browser stream view, so a WeChat voice call or voice note needs a human speaking through that view. It cannot be fully automated.

Typing Chinese characters through the keyboard endpoint is not documented. It is probably fine, since the DroidRun Portal keyboard historically sends text directly, but this is unverified. Test it in the first hour. Fallback: set the clipboard and paste.
Triggers have no documented filter for app notifications by package or text, so a new WeChat message has to be detected by polling (Mobilerun cron flow or Naive cron), not pushed.

Installing apps on cloud Android: the docs only cover APK upload. Play Store sign-in and install appear only in a marketing comparison page. Installing WeChat from the Play Store needs a Google account on the device, so budget time for it.
Latency and cost: each step takes time and about 0.5 credits. No per-step latency is published. Expect several seconds per step, so roughly 30-90 seconds per WeChat send (an estimate).
The status page shows all components operational but no uptime history, so reliability is unproven. Keep a recorded fallback demo.

Mobilerun's hackathon blog says you 'link your Mobilerun API key to Naive', which suggests Mobilerun powers it, but that is an inference.
key_capabilities: Actions: screenshot, element_tree, tap (by x/y or by a selector on text, resource_id or content_desc), type, press_key, scroll, open_url, launch_app, install_app, end

Config: platform (android or ios); os_version (13, 14 or 15); jurisdiction (us, eu or as, meaning the US, Germany or Singapore, with a matching residential IP, GPS, timezone and carrier); idle_timeout_minutes (1-180); max_duration_minutes (up to 60 for agents); apps (up to 10 catalogue package or bundle IDs)
Live view in the Naive chat's Computer panel, plus POST /v1/mobile_devices/{id}/live_view
Permission gating per tool (allow, ask or deny; ask is the default), which suits human-in-the-loop
tools.api_and_setup: Enable it in the Naive agent definition: tools.configs.mobile {enabled, permission, config: {platform, jurisdiction, apps}}. It requires the 'pi' harness and a deployment that can provision phones; otherwise you get 501 feature_not_configured. Cost is $0.05 per minute for Android and $0.08 per minute for iOS, charged to the organisation balance and not counted against the session budget. REST: POST /v1/mobile_devices returns 202 (then poll until ready), POST /v1/mobile_devices/{id}/act, DELETE /v1/mobile_devices/{id}. Creating a device requires enough balance for 10 minutes.
tools.role_in_product: Phone access from inside a Naive agent with no integration work. It is good for stateless jobs: browsing the Alibaba.com or AliExpress app without logging in, checking listings, or a quick demo of the agent using a phone natively in Naive.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: Not suitable for WeChat. The phone is temporary: there is no pause or snapshot, and 'When the session ends, the device ends with it.' Apps come only from the platform catalogue, with no upload and no store account. A WeChat login (QR or friend verification, then a persistent session) cannot survive between sessions, and logging the same account onto a fresh device each time is itself a strong ban signal. Use this tool for one-shot catalogue browsing. Use Mobilerun Cloud directly for the persistent WeChat and Alibaba messenger phone.
limitations_risks: Phones do not persist across sessions; an agent's phone lives at most 60 minutes.

Apps come only from the catalogue. WhatsApp, Instagram, TikTok, Spotify and Firefox are confirmed; WeChat, Alibaba.com and 1688 are unknown. install_app returns 400 within seconds for apps not in the catalogue, which makes it a quick availability check.
On iOS, element_tree and selector taps usually return 400, open_url returns 400, and launch_app can return 409 after 30 seconds.
First boot can take up to about 2.5 minutes on Android and about 3 minutes on iOS.
verified_facts: The mobile tool gives one phone per session that closes on end, on session end or on idle. It costs $0.05 per minute on Android and $0.08 per minute on iOS, with jurisdictions us, eu and as (https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/tools.md)

'When the session ends, the device ends with it'. There is no pause, snapshot or keep-alive, and apps come from the platform catalogue only, with no store account (https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/mobile-devices.md ; https://usenaive.ai/docs/computer/mobile.md)
The Naive docs never mention Mobilerun (https://usenaive.ai/docs/llms.txt)
unverified_or_inferred: Whether Naive's mobile tool is backed by Mobilerun, and whether linking a Mobilerun API key routes it to your own Mobilerun devices or minutes. Confirm with Naive or Mobilerun staff.
Whether WeChat or the Alibaba.com app (com.alibaba.intl.android.apps.poseidon) is in the Naive app catalogue. Test with install_app.

tools.name: Integration glue: Mobilerun MCP as a Naive MCP connector (with vault credential)
tools.what_it_is: The recommended way to connect Mobilerun to a Naive agent: declare Mobilerun's hosted MCP server in the agent's mcp_servers, and store the dr_sk_ key as a Naive vault credential that Naive injects server-side.
key_capabilities: Naive agent JSON: mcp_servers: [{type: 'url', name: 'mobilerun', url: 'https://api.mobilerun.ai/v1/mcp'}]
Per-tool gating, e.g. tools.configs['mobilerun.run_task'] = {enabled: true, permission: 'allow'}. Keep message-sending tools on 'ask' as a natural approval gate.
Auth: a static_bearer vault credential, matched to the server URL and injected when the session starts. Naive rejects inline Authorization headers.
Up to 20 MCP servers per agent and 100 tools per server; Mobilerun has 39.
If the server is unreachable, Naive emits session.degraded (mcp_server_unavailable) and retries on the next wake instead of crashing.
tools.api_and_setup:
1. Get a dr_sk_ key, ideally the one with the hackathon minutes.
2. Create a Naive vault credential of type static_bearer, bound to https://api.mobilerun.ai/v1/mcp.
3. Add the MCP server to the agent and allow mobilerun.run_task, get_task, get_task_media, get_device_ui_state, get_device_screenshot, device_action, manage_device_files and send_task_message.
4. Write a skill or system prompt with the WeChat standard operating procedure.

Alternatives:
(a) Run a small Node script with @mobilerun/sdk via bash in Naive's Computer sandbox. Vault secret substitution for sandbox traffic is 'coming soon', so the key would have to sit in the sandbox.
(b) Run a small webhook service (for example on Render or Vercel) that receives Mobilerun task.run.completed webhooks and posts into the Naive session via Naive webhooks or cron.

Naive's custom client-executed function tools are listed as 'Coming soon', so MCP is the supported path today.
tools.role_in_product: Mobilerun appears as first-class tools for the Naive procurement agent. The coordinator or an outreach teammate calls mobilerun.run_task with an outputSchema and gets structured supplier replies back in the same session, where Naive's event stream, budgets and audit log capture everything.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: Every WeChat or Alibaba-app action becomes a Naive tool call. Naive's per-tool 'ask' permission (the session pauses in requires_action until a tool.confirm event) and its ask_operator tool give the founder an approval step before the final 'proceed' message. Naive cron can run 'check WeChat inbox' sweeps overnight Shenzhen time.
limitations_risks: Mobile tasks run from 30 seconds to 45 minutes. run_task returns immediately, so the agent must poll get_task or wait for a webhook. Budget the extra tool calls.
Naive MCP tools default to 'ask'. If you forget to set them to allow, autonomous runs stall, which hurts the 'runs without humans' score.
This combination is untested. Do a 30-minute smoke test first: list_devices, then a run_task that opens Settings.
verified_facts: Naive MCP syntax uses mcp_servers entries of type url. Inline secret-bearing headers are rejected, and auth comes from a vault credential (static_bearer or mcp_oauth) matched by URL. MCP tools default to ask. Limits are 20 servers per agent and 100 tools per server (https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/tools.md)
Naive custom function tools are listed as 'Coming soon' (https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/tools.md)
Vault secret substitution is live on the MCP connector path, with all sandbox traffic 'coming soon' (https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/identity.md)

Naive has an ask_operator tool (the session reports awaiting_answer) and an 'ask' permission per tool (the session pauses in requires_action until a tool.confirm event) (https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/tools.md)
Mobilerun's MCP endpoint uses Bearer auth (https://docs.mobilerun.ai/mcp-server.md)
unverified_or_inferred: That a static_bearer vault credential is sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>', which Mobilerun expects. Very likely but untested.
Whether the hackathon's built-in 'link your Mobilerun key to Naive' flow makes this connector unnecessary.

tools.name: WeChat channel driven by Mobilerun (real iPhone or connected personal Android phone)
tools.what_it_is: Not a sponsor product but the target channel. Chinese factory sales reps actually use personal WeChat, and it has no official send/receive API for personal accounts. UI automation on a phone is the only realistic way for an agent to use it.
key_capabilities: Send and read text in existing chats: open a chat by the contact's remark name and read message bubbles from the accessibility tree on Android, or from screenshots with vision on iOS.

Add a supplier: search their WeChat ID or phone number, tap Add to Contacts, and include a verification note. Or upload their QR image to the phone gallery (Mobilerun manage_device_files or upload-file) and use WeChat's Scan, then Album. The supplier has to accept.
Receive files such as spec sheets, proforma invoices and photos; read them by screenshot or download them via the device files API.
Supplier voice notes: long-press, then Convert to Text, lets the agent read them. This is based on the standard WeChat feature and is untested here.
Voice calls: the agent can start a call by tapping, but the audio has to come from a human via Mobilerun's browser stream view (call media). There is no API for injecting audio.
tools.api_and_setup:
Account: use an established WeChat account a teammate already owns (registered for a while, with friends). A brand-new account needs an existing eligible user to scan a QR code to verify it, has limits on adding friends (sources cite roughly 5-10 active adds a day for accounts under 3 months old), and triggers risk-control prompts.

Device options, safest first:
1. A teammate's real Android phone connected through the Mobilerun Portal APK (Personal Phone, $5 per month; turn on the accessibility service and display-over-other-apps). It is real hardware and the account's usual phone, but it must stay online.
2. A Mobilerun real physical iPhone (first come, first served at the hackathon). Log WeChat in by phone number plus SMS, or by QR from the existing device. Only one phone can be logged in at a time, so this logs out the teammate's phone. You will probably need vision mode.
3. A Mobilerun virtual Android Phone. Highest ban risk, because WeChat bans emulators.

Practices:
- One account per device; no VPN hopping; keep a stable residential IP.
- Set humanize=true and leave at least 5-10 seconds between messages, with only a few dozen messages a day.
- Never mass-add contacts; prefer that suppliers scan our QR code.
- Write natural, individually composed Chinese messages (LLM-generated, not templated blasts).
- Have a human approve the first message to each new supplier.
tools.role_in_product: The highest-signal outreach channel for Chinese factories, and the most impressive demo: the agent messages a real Shenzhen supplier on WeChat on Saturday evening, and real replies arrive overnight.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: This is the core of the route. Alibaba.com or 1688 handles discovery and first contact; many suppliers share a WeChat ID after an initial Alibaba Messenger exchange (an inference). WeChat then carries the conversation about specs, MOQ, price and lead time. Mobilerun polling extracts the replies into structured JSON for the decision memo. After the founder says 'proceed', the agent sends the confirmation and the request for samples and a shipping schedule over WeChat.
limitations_risks: WeChat's help center lists 'Using an Android emulator ... or other non-official plugins to run WeChat' and 'Using a virtual phone number to register' as reasons to block accounts. A permanent block for breaking the terms of service cannot be lifted.

New accounts usually need a friend to scan a verification QR code, and face strict limits on adding friends. A 2026 Chinese blog reports a WeChat Security Center notice that names automation scripts and bulk-add tools as targets (secondary source).
Only one phone can be logged in at a time, so moving a teammate's account to a cloud phone logs out their own phone. Recovering the account may need help from another WeChat user.
The demo depends on suppliers accepting friend requests within hours. Before Saturday, make sure 2-3 friendly contacts or real suppliers are already in the contact list.
Voice calls and voice notes cannot be fully automated via the API; they need a human in the stream view.
On iOS, WeChat has no accessibility tree, so the agent relies on vision. That means slower, costlier steps and possible misreading of Chinese text; cross-check with a second screenshot pass.
verified_facts: WeChat's reasons for blocking accounts include using an Android emulator or non-official plugins, and registering with a virtual phone number (https://help.wechat.com/cgi-bin/micromsg-bin/oshelpcenter?opcode=2&id=120813euejvf150504mfan7b&t=help_center%2Fw_topic_detail)

New WeChat accounts are often asked to have an eligible existing user scan a verification QR code, and VoIP or virtual numbers are often blocked (https://chinaneighbor.com/guide/essentials/wechat-for-foreigners-guide-2026/ ; https://ltl-school.com/how-to-use-wechat/)

Logging into the same WeChat account on a second phone usually logs out the first, while a phone and a PC can be logged in at the same time (https://multilogin.com/blog/how-to-manage-multiple-wechat-accounts/ ; https://blog.omnichat.ai/one-device-two-wechat-accounts/)

Chinese practitioner sources rate UI automation as a lower ban risk than hook or protocol bots. Bans are driven by message frequency, account age and the environment, such as emulators or rooted phones (https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/1891472259190862807 ; https://linux.do/t/topic/1785134 ; https://www.v2ex.com/t/868138)

Guidance for new accounts is about 5-10 friend adds a day for accounts under 3 months old, and letting others scan your QR code is safer (https://blog.csdn.net/2402_86571652/article/details/158922424 ; https://www.zhanghaobang.cn/policy/wechat-anti-ban-guide-2026)

The Mobilerun Portal APK needs the accessibility service and display-over-other-apps, on Android 8 or later. The connected phone appears as a Personal Phone (https://docs.mobilerun.ai/guides/connect-android.md)

Connecting your own iPhone needs iOS 27 or later via Chrome or Edge over USB, or iOS 16 or later via the mobilerun-ios CLI on a Mac. The host computer must stay connected (https://docs.mobilerun.ai/guides/connect-iphone.md)
unverified_or_inferred: No public report was found, positive or negative, of WeChat running on Mobilerun specifically.
Whether WeChat detects an enabled third-party accessibility service such as Mobilerun Portal. No hard evidence either way.
Whether a Mobilerun connected-phone slot is included in the hackathon credits.
Whether WeChat's Convert to Text works on supplier voice notes in this setup.

tools.name: Mobilerun open-source framework (formerly DroidRun) + mobile-harness skill
tools.what_it_is: The MIT-licensed Python agent framework (pip or uv package 'mobilerun', run with mobilerun run "..."). It drives a local Android device over ADB using the Portal APK, or iOS via mobilerun-ios (WebDriverAgent or native control). It works with any LLM: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama, DeepSeek and others. The mobile-harness skill teaches coding agents to use mobilerun_core against cloud or local devices.
key_capabilities: Local control of a teammate's physical phone, using no cloud minutes
Vision and vision-only modes, reasoning (a manager/executor setup), structured output, custom tools, app instruction cards, credentials, tracing (Phoenix and Langfuse) and macro replay
mobilerun_core backends: cloud, local-android-adb, local-android-http and local-ios-http
tools.api_and_setup: Install with uv tool install mobilerun, then run mobilerun setup (installs Portal and enables accessibility), mobilerun ping, mobilerun configure, and mobilerun run "...". Needs Python 3.11-3.13. Install the harness with npx skills add droidrun/mobile-harness. The PyPI package mobilerun is at 0.7.4.
tools.role_in_product: Fallback if cloud minutes or iPhones run out, or if the WeChat account has to stay on the teammate's own physical phone. It runs on a laptop next to the phone and can use OpenRouter (a sponsor) for the model.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: The lowest-ban-risk WeChat setup: a real phone, a real account, local USB. A WeChat app instruction card (how to open a chat, where the input box is, how to read bubbles) improves reliability. Naive's cloud cannot reach it without a public tunnel, so if allowed, a Mobilerun Cloud Personal Phone connected through Portal is the better bridge.
limitations_risks: It runs locally, so the laptop and phone must stay on overnight to catch Shenzhen replies.
Exposing it to Naive needs a public HTTPS MCP or webhook wrapper, because Naive refuses localhost and private MCP URLs.
verified_facts: The framework supports real Android devices and emulators, real iOS devices via mobilerun-ios, and the iOS Simulator. It installs with uv tool install mobilerun and does not support Python 3.14 (https://github.com/droidrun/mobilerun)
mobile-harness backends are cloud, local-android-adb, local-android-http and local-ios-http (https://docs.mobilerun.ai/skills/mobile-harness.md)
Naive MCP URLs must be public HTTPS; localhost and private IPs are refused (https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/tools.md)
unverified_or_inferred: The benchmark claims (the README's 91.4% badge, 100% on AndroidWorld and 98.34% on iOSWorld) are reported by the vendor.

key_findings: Mobilerun is DroidRun renamed (Droidrun GmbH; repo github.com/droidrun/mobilerun, MIT, about 10k stars). It is a hosted fleet of virtual Android phones and real physical iPhones that agents drive. Interfaces: REST (https://api.mobilerun.ai/v1, Bearer dr_sk_ key), TypeScript SDK @mobilerun/sdk v6.1.0, Python mobilerun-sdk 6.1.0, the open-source framework pip mobilerun 0.7.4, and a hosted MCP server at https://api.mobilerun.ai/v1/mcp with 39 tools.

There are two control levels. (1) POST /v1/tasks takes a natural-language task, which Mobilerun's own agent executes using its model catalog: mobile-agent-fast/thinking, Claude, Gemini, GPT, Kimi. Options include outputSchema for JSON results, systemPrompt, maxSteps and executionTimeout up to 45 minutes, with status, trajectory and screenshots returned. (2) Low-level endpoints: tap, swipe, keyboard, clipboard, deep link, install/start app, upload file, screenshot, and ui-state (an accessibility tree with text, resourceId and bounds).

Persistence is good on Mobilerun: Android Phones are 'dedicated, persistent', and a stopped device keeps its apps, logins and identity without being billed. Naive's own built-in `mobile` tool is the opposite. It is temporary, the device ends with the session, there is no pause, and apps come only from a catalogue with no store account. So a logged-in WeChat or Alibaba messenger phone must live in Mobilerun, not in Naive's mobile tool.

Correction to our prior assumptions: Naive does have a built-in `mobile` tool (cloud Android/iPhone, $0.05 or $0.08 per minute), MCP connectors with vault-injected credentials, a per-tool 'ask' permission (the session pauses in requires_action until confirmed with tool.confirm), and an ask_operator tool. So there IS a human-in-the-loop primitive for the founder approval step. Naive's custom function tools are 'coming soon', so MCP is the way to plug Mobilerun in.

The recommended integration is to declare Mobilerun's MCP in the Naive agent's mcp_servers with url https://api.mobilerun.ai/v1/mcp. Store the dr_sk_ key as a static_bearer vault credential, because Naive rejects inline Authorization headers. Set mobilerun.run_task, get_task, get_device_ui_state and the other needed tools to 'allow', and keep message-sending on 'ask' until the founder approves. Use Mobilerun webhooks or Naive cron for overnight polling. Estimated effort is about 2 hours.

Hackathon allowance (verified on Mobilerun's blog): 72 hours of Android and iOS device minutes, 6 seats, iPhones first come, first served. You claim it with the event QR code and then link your Mobilerun API key to Naive. Judging emphasis: a working end-to-end workflow, not an agent that explains what it would do. Normal pricing: Free tier 60 minutes and 500 credits; about 0.5 credits ($0.005) per agent step; $0.03 per minute overage; iPhone add-on $200 per month.

Biggest WeChat risk: WeChat's help center lists 'Using an Android emulator ... or non-official plugins' and virtual phone numbers as reasons to block accounts. Mobilerun's own docs call its Android Phone a 'virtual Android device' (EU region), and only its iPhones are called physical. So put WeChat on a real iPhone (claim one early, since they are first come) or on a teammate's real Android phone connected via the Mobilerun Portal APK. Do not use a virtual Android.

WeChat account reality: brand-new accounts, especially foreign or VoIP-number ones, usually need an existing eligible WeChat user to scan a verification QR code, and face limits of roughly 5-10 friend adds a day plus risk-control checks. Only one phone can be logged in at a time. Use an established teammate account, pre-seed 2-3 supplier or friendly contacts before Saturday, pace messages at least 5-10 seconds apart with humanize=true, avoid VPN hopping, and prefer that suppliers scan our QR code.

Feasibility of WeChat actions through Mobilerun. Sending and reading text, and opening chats, work through ordinary UI automation; there is no WeChat-specific guide and no public report either way. Adding a supplier works by WeChat ID or phone search plus a verification note, or by uploading their QR image to the gallery and using Scan, then Album. Voice notes can probably be read by long-pressing and choosing Convert to Text (an inference). Voice calls and sent voice notes cannot be automated: audio injection exists only as browser 'call media' in the Cloud stream view, with no API, so a call needs a human speaking.

The Alibaba.com app is explicitly supported. Mobilerun has an Alibaba app-agent guide and a procurement solution page: it signs in to Alibaba and 1688, reads the supplier inbox and messenger, extracts unit price, MOQ, lead time and payment terms as JSON, and drafts counter-offers for approval. That makes Alibaba app chat the safer, lower-risk mobile demo, with WeChat as the stretch goal.

Operational gotchas. One task per device: a queued task fails after a 30-second contention timeout. Tasks are capped at 2,700 seconds. Chinese text input via the keyboard endpoint is undocumented, so test it early, with set-clipboard then paste as the fallback. iOS often has no accessibility tree (DEVICE_TOOL_UNSUPPORTED), so WeChat on an iPhone needs vision=true. There are no app-notification triggers filtered by package, so detect replies by polling. The status page shows no uptime history, so record a fallback demo video.

How to win Best Mobile Automation:
- Show a full loop running unattended on real apps. The Naive coordinator finds suppliers (web plus the Alibaba app), Mobilerun sends a personalised Chinese RFQ via the Alibaba app and WeChat, and overnight polling extracts the replies into JSON.
- Naive writes the decision memo, with the trajectory screenshots as evidence, and asks the founder via ask_operator.
- On 'proceed', Mobilerun sends the sample and shipping request.
- Embed the live Mobilerun device stream in our dashboard (the embed-device-stream guide), and show 2 phones in parallel (Alibaba app plus WeChat).
- Use outputSchema and webhooks, and show real supplier replies received overnight.
- Mention cost per supplier contacted (steps × $0.005).

tools.name: Alibaba.com Message Center + RFQ (driven by a browser agent or the Alibaba app on a Mobilerun phone)
tools.what_it_is: Alibaba.com's built-in buyer and supplier messaging (message.alibaba.com, the 'Contact Supplier' inquiry form, and chat in the Alibaba.com app), plus the free RFQ board where suppliers bid on a posted request. This is where most export-oriented Chinese electronics and ODM suppliers expect a first contact.
key_capabilities: Contact Supplier inquiry on any product page, which lands in the supplier's Message Center or Workbench client
RFQ: post one spec and receive bids from many suppliers (about 10 to 15 quotes on Alibaba's own figures), at no cost
Supplier signals on each storefront: Verified / Gold Supplier, years on platform, response rate, response time, Trade Assurance limit
Trade Assurance protects only orders paid through Alibaba checkout; on-platform messages serve as dispute evidence
Accio Work / Accio Sourcing Toolkit (Alibaba's own AI agent) already does RFQ, bulk outreach and multi-round negotiation through this same messaging system, with human approval gates
tools.api_and_setup: I found NO public buyer-side messaging, inquiry or RFQ API. The Alibaba.com Open Platform (openapi.alibaba.com) lists System auth (/auth/token/create, /auth/token/refresh), Product, and Buyer/Seller Transaction & Fulfillment groups. Access needs GGS developer registration, app review by GGS admins, then per-API permission. I found no chat or IM endpoints. The only realistic hackathon path is UI automation of a real buyer account: either the Naive Computer browser logged into alibaba.com (expect captchas and slider challenges), or the Alibaba.com Android/iOS app on a Mobilerun device. The RFQ is free; paid add-ons are $9.99 Urgent and $2.99 Extra Quotes. Setup: create the buyer account by hand before the event, log in once by hand, then have the agent read and reply in the Message Center.
tools.role_in_product: Primary discovery and first-contact channel. The Sourcing agent searches, shortlists by supplier signals, sends structured inquiries (specs, MOQ, unit price at 500/1k/5k, lead time, CE/FCC/RoHS, sample cost, FOB Shenzhen), and posts one RFQ to collect inbound quotes. The Negotiator agent continues the thread. After the founder approves, the Executor agent requests a sample order or Trade Assurance order link. A human always clicks Pay, which also matches Accio's own design.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: This is the on-ramp to WeChat. Suppliers routinely offer their WeChat or WhatsApp ID in Alibaba chat ('add my WeChat for faster reply'). The agent captures that ID and hands off to the WeChat route, while keeping binding terms (price, spec, payment) on Alibaba for Trade Assurance evidence. It is also the most reliable source of REAL replies inside a 22-hour window.
limitations_risks: ToS: Alibaba-family terms prohibit 'systematic retrieval ... whether through robots, spiders, automatic devices' without written permission and allow suspension of the account 'and any and all accounts determined to be related'. Low-volume messaging by an agent on one real account is a grey area; bulk scraping is clearly prohibited. Moderate risk of a buyer-account restriction.
Anti-bot: captchas, slider challenges and login risk checks on the web. Alibaba reportedly challenges non-browser traffic. The mobile app via Mobilerun is likely less fragile (inferred).
Timing: Saturday and Sunday SF hacking hours map to Chinese Sunday and very early Monday, so many reps are off. Auto-replies and weekend-working sales reps exist, but volume will be lower.
Alibaba may mask or warn about off-platform contact details in chat (inferred, not verified).
Off-platform payment voids Trade Assurance.
verified_facts: Buyers contact suppliers via 'Contact Supplier'; messages live in My Alibaba Message Center (message.alibaba.com), and Alibaba advises keeping 100% of communication there for Trade Assurance - https://smartbuy.alibaba.com/buyingguides/how-to-contact-alibaba

RFQ: buyers can get up to 15 quotes from qualified suppliers, posting is free; each RFQ can be answered by up to 10 sellers - https://activity.alibaba.com/ggs/your_step_by_step_guide_to_using_our_request_for_quotation_tool.html
RFQ paid add-ons: $9.99 Urgent Request, $2.99 Extra Quotes - https://cnbusinesshub.com/corporate_advisory/article-09-alibaba-rfq-2026-0727.html

Trade Assurance applies to transactions paid through Alibaba's supported payment process; direct bank transfers may not qualify - https://seller.alibaba.com/businessblogs/alibaba-trade-assurance-how-order-protection-works-for-buyers-and-sellers-px002dpu1

That the mobile app on Mobilerun is less captcha-prone than web is an inference.
Whether Alibaba chat masks WeChat IDs or phone numbers today is unverified.

Accio is a competitor and benchmark. Judges may ask 'why not Accio?'. Our differentiator: multi-channel (WeChat, email, voice), a hard authority and budget envelope, a founder approval memo, and a generalized 'outside-world department' beyond Alibaba.

tools.name: Email (via AgentMail, Naive Identity email, or any inbox API)
tools.what_it_is: Plain email to supplier sales addresses. These are found on Made-in-China / Global Sources profiles, supplier websites, catalog PDFs, or given in Alibaba chat. Common supplier domains: company domains, QQ Mail, 163.com, aliyun mail.
key_capabilities: Fully API-driven send and receive, threading, attachments (spec sheet PDF, NDA, PO)
Formal record of terms; sourcing guides recommend email as the system of record and WeChat for speed
No platform ToS issue when writing to a published business address
tools.api_and_setup: Use a sponsor inbox API (AgentMail) or Naive Identity email. Budget about 1 to 2 hours: a custom domain with SPF/DKIM, outbound send, and an inbound webhook into the Naive session. Deliverability to Chinese providers (QQ/163) from a brand-new domain is uncertain. Use a warmed or real domain where possible, plain text, and no link-heavy bodies (inferred).
tools.role_in_product: Default async channel and system of record for every supplier. The decision memo cites email-confirmed terms. After 'proceed', the Executor sends a formal sample request or PO email with the shipping schedule.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: Parallel to WeChat. Every WeChat or Alibaba agreement gets mirrored into an email confirmation ('per our WeChat conversation, confirming: 2 samples at $35 each incl. DHL, ship by Nov 14'). It is also the fallback when a supplier won't add a foreign WeChat.
limitations_risks: Slower than WeChat. Guides claim WeChat replies come in under 2 hours versus about 24 hours for email (vendor claim).
Spam filtering at QQ/163 for new domains (inferred).
Finding direct emails needs scraping (Apify) or B2B directories, and scraping carries its own ToS concerns.
Bulk cold email: CAN-SPAM applies on the US side. Low legal risk at hackathon volume.
verified_facts: Sourcing guides advise using WeChat for relationship/speed but email as the system of record for contractual obligations - https://stypewriter.com/china-communicating/
Advice to ask suppliers which channel they prefer; email is almost always viable - https://www.feedbackwhiz.com/blog/10-tips-for-great-communication-with-chinese-suppliers/
unverified_or_inferred: Deliverability to QQ/163 for new sending domains was not tested.
Response-time comparison is from sourcing vendors, not measured data.

tools.name: WeChat personal account operated on a real phone (Mobilerun UI automation)
tools.what_it_is: A normal personal WeChat (Weixin) account, registered by a human on a real phone, that an agent drives by tapping the real WeChat app on a Mobilerun device. No protocol hacks; it reads chats and types replies through the UI.
key_capabilities: Reaches suppliers on the channel nearly every Chinese factory sales rep actually uses
Add a supplier by WeChat ID or by scanning the QR the supplier shares; send text, images and spec PDFs; voice notes are possible
Visible 'agent operating a real phone' demo, which fits the Mobilerun 'Best Mobile Automation' track
tools.api_and_setup: No official API for personal WeChat. Setup: register a WeChat account BEFORE the hackathon on a real phone number (not VoIP). New accounts need friend QR verification (helper account age at least 1 to 6 months, limited helps per year) or payment-card verification. Avoid VPN during registration. Log the account in on the Mobilerun device. Have the agent use screen reading plus tap and type to open chats, read new messages, translate, and reply. Ask suppliers to add YOU (share your QR or ID in Alibaba chat) rather than mass-adding them, because rapid adds get new accounts flagged.
tools.role_in_product: The high-touch negotiation channel. Once a supplier shares a WeChat ID, the Negotiator moves there and conducts bilingual (Chinese and English) negotiation within the authority envelope. After the founder says 'proceed', it sends the confirmation and sample or shipping next steps on WeChat and mirrors them to email.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: This IS the WeChat route. It is the most authentic and judge-impressive channel. Suppliers answer WeChat on weekends far more readily than email. That matters because all hackathon hours fall on Chinese Sunday and very early Monday morning.
limitations_risks: ToS: WeChat forbids third-party plugins and unofficial tools. A paying PadLocal user received a WeChat warning for 'third-party software, plug-ins and other unofficial tools'. UI automation on a real device is lower risk than protocol bots, but not zero. Community reports say bans cluster around hook-based tools and mass messaging.
Account bootstrap: friend verification is required. Do it before Nov 7; a fresh account that adds many contacts quickly gets flagged.
Mobilerun device availability (iPhones first-come) and UI-automation brittleness: popups, Chinese UI strings, keyboard IME.
Mainland data rules: messages are on Tencent servers. Fine for demo data; note it for real customers.
Only use a dedicated test account, never a team member's personal WeChat.
verified_facts: Virtually every export-facing factory sales rep uses WeChat as primary channel; suppliers commonly ask to move from Alibaba to WeChat - https://leighsourcing.com/connect-with-chinese-suppliers-on-wechat/ and https://yansourcing.com/how-to-contact-chinese-suppliers/

New WeChat accounts generally require friend QR verification; VoIP numbers often fail; helper account limits; VPN during registration gets flagged; adding too many people quickly gets flagged - https://chinaneighbor.com/guide/essentials/wechat-for-foreigners-guide-2026/ and https://ltl-school.com/how-to-use-wechat/
WeChat warned a PadLocal user about third-party/unofficial tools (Jan 2025) - https://github.com/wechaty/puppet-supports/issues/626

2026 survey: bans more commonly reported for hook-based tools than pure UI automation; low-volume personal use ban probability relatively low - https://yage.ai/share/wechat-uia-platform-feasibility-survey-en-20260327.html

tools.name: WeCom (Enterprise WeChat) - WeChat Customer Service (微信客服) API and External Contacts
tools.what_it_is: Tencent's official enterprise product that interoperates with personal WeChat. 微信客服 lets any WeChat user open a chat with a company service account through a link or QR. The company replies via the official API (qyapi.weixin.qq.com). External Contacts lets employees add WeChat users as customers.
key_capabilities: kf/send_msg: API-sent text, image, file, link, menu and location messages to a WeChat user who messaged first: up to 5 messages within 48 hours, and each new customer message re-opens the window
kf/sync_msg with callback (kf_msg_or_event): pull inbound supplier messages, last 3 days, cursor-based
externalcontact/add_msg_template: mass message to external WeChat contacts, but the member MUST confirm in the WeCom client before it sends; capped per customer per month
WeChat users chat with WeCom without installing WeCom; 'Contact Me' QR adds the company to their contacts
tools.api_and_setup: Register at work.weixin.qq.com on the web; an overseas phone number is allowed. Create a self-built app, add it to '微信客服-可调用接口的应用', and set the kf account to API management. Configure a callback URL with token and AES key, which is a public HTTPS endpoint (Vercel or Render works). Get an access_token (corpid + secret), create a kf account, and get its link (work.weixin.qq.com/kfid/...). Verification is optional. Overseas verification is reportedly RMB 700/yr (some 2026 sources say no fee) and takes 1 to 15 business days, so it is NOT achievable during the hackathon. Unverified orgs reportedly can serve only 100 customers in total via 微信客服, which is enough for a demo. Since Dec 2023 the system app secret can't call kf APIs; use a self-built app secret.
tools.role_in_product: The compliant, API-first WeChat path. The agent pastes its kf link or QR into Alibaba chat or email ('chat with our sourcing desk on WeChat'). When the supplier taps it, every subsequent message flows through the official API into the Naive session, with no phone automation and no ban risk.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: The best 'legit at scale' WeChat story for the 'Most likely to scale' judges. It complements the Mobilerun personal-account demo: phone automation for the wow, WeCom for the production architecture slide. Constraint: the supplier must initiate. You cannot cold-message an arbitrary WeChat ID via API, and free-form 1:1 sends to External Contacts need a human-confirmed client action.
limitations_risks: Supplier must click the link or scan the QR first. Cold suppliers may not; the conversion rate is unknown.
5 messages per 48h per inbound message. Fine for negotiation cadence, but the agent must batch content.
Unverified org: reportedly 100 total customers via 微信客服, and error '8-主体未验证' exists as a send-failure reason. Unclear exactly which features need verification.
Callback endpoint must answer WeCom's URL verification handshake (AES). The fiddly part is 1 to 2 hours.
Messages display as a business service account, which some suppliers may trust less than a personal contact (inferred).
ToS risk: low. This is official API use.
verified_facts: kf/send_msg: POST https://qyapi.weixin.qq.com/cgi-bin/kf/send_msg; customer must message first; 48h window, max 5 messages; supported msgtypes text/image/voice/video/file/link/miniprogram/msgmenu/location; system app secret disallowed since 2023-12-01 - https://developer.work.weixin.qq.com/document/path/94677
kf/sync_msg + kf_msg_or_event callback; only last 3 days of messages; send-failure reasons include '8-主体未验证', '6-超过5条限制', '4-会话已过期' - https://developer.work.weixin.qq.com/document/path/94670

key_findings: RANKED CHANNEL RECOMMENDATION for a 22h demo with REAL supplier replies. (1) Alibaba.com Message Center plus one free RFQ: must. It has the highest real-reply probability (about 10 to 15 RFQ quotes is Alibaba's own figure), but it requires UI automation because no buyer messaging API exists. ToS risk is moderate: an automated-access clause plus account suspension. (2) Email via AgentMail or Naive Identity: must. It is the system of record and has low ToS risk. (3) WeChat personal account driven on a real phone via Mobilerun: must for the Mobile track and the core story. ToS and ban risk is low-to-moderate at low volume; the account must be pre-registered and friend-verified. (4) WeCom 微信客服 official API: should. It is the compliant scalable WeChat path, but the supplier must click your link first, and you get 5 msgs per 48h per inbound message. (5) Made-in-China / Global Sources inquiries: should. (6) WhatsApp Cloud API: nice. It is blocked in mainland China, so suppliers need a VPN. (7) Twilio voice to China at $0.312/min: nice; use it only for pre-arranged calls. Skip Wechaty/PadLocal (defunct and ban-prone), WeChat Official Accounts (7 to 15 day verification), and AliExpress/DHgate for outreach.

There is NO official API to cold-message an arbitrary WeChat user. WeCom's add_msg_template only queues a mass message that a human member must confirm in the client. 微信客服 kf/send_msg only works after the WeChat user messages first (48h window, max 5 messages). Personal WeChat automation is either unofficial protocol bots (bans reported, PadLocal unmaintained since 2022) or real-device UI automation, which is the Mobilerun angle.

A practical WeChat funnel: the agent makes first contact in Alibaba chat or email, asks 'what's your WeChat?' or offers our WeChat QR or WeCom kf link, and the supplier adds us. Suppliers frequently propose moving to WeChat themselves. Keep price, spec and payment terms mirrored on Alibaba or email for Trade Assurance evidence; WeChat agreements are not enforced by Alibaba.

Alibaba's own Accio Work / Accio Sourcing Toolkit (Mar and Jul 2026) already does RFQs, bulk outreach and multi-round negotiation through Alibaba messaging, with human approval for financial actions. Expect judges to ask 'how is this different?'. Answer: multi-channel (WeChat, email, voice), multi-marketplace, explicit authority/budget envelopes, founder decision memo and proceed loop, generalizes to sourcing humans, and fully autonomous company integration via Naive.

TIMING (verified arithmetic, US DST ended Nov 1 2026): PST is UTC-8 and Shenzhen is UTC+8, so 16h ahead. All hackathon hours (Sat Nov 7 to Sun Nov 8, SF) fall on Chinese SUNDAY Nov 8 and the early hours of Monday Nov 9. Sat 6pm SF = Sun 10am Shenzhen; Sun 9am SF = Mon 1am Shenzhen. Expect weekend-reduced responsiveness. Send outreach as early as rules allow on Saturday so it lands in Chinese Sunday daytime. WeChat gets weekend replies more than email (inferred). Have a pre-arranged friendly supplier or sourcing contact as a demo backstop.

NEGOTIATION NORMS for the agent's authority envelope (verified across 2026 sourcing guides): the standard first order is 30% T/T deposit and 70% before shipment. Push for 70% against passed pre-shipment inspection or a B/L copy. Milestone 30/40/30 is suggested for $20k to $100k. Never demand payment after receipt (a red flag to factories). Sample fees are often refundable against the first bulk order, so ask. Tooling can be split from the product deposit. Terms improve to 20/80, then Net 30/60 with order history. Quote basis should be FOB Shenzhen (or EXW/DDP) with an explicit Incoterm.

VETTING CHECKLIST to encode: Alibaba Verified/Gold Supplier, years on platform, response rate and time, Trade Assurance limit. Made-in-China Audited Supplier report (SGS/BV/TUV, free to buyers). Global Sources Verified Manufacturer. Cross-check the business license on gsxt.gov.cn. Third-party inspection (QIMA/SGS/V-Trust) for orders over $5k. Red flag: requests to wire to a private or offshore account 'to save fees'. Trade Assurance covers only on-platform payments.

Fall-detection inquiry template should ask for: device type (pendant, wristband, or module); IMU part (e.g. accelerometer/gyro model); connectivity (BLE / LoRa / 4G LTE-M with SOS call); battery life; IP rating; ODM/OEM customization and private label; MOQ; unit price at 500/1k/5k; sample price and lead time; mass-production lead time; CE/FCC/RoHS (and FDA if positioned as medical; inferred) certificates as PDFs; FOB Shenzhen; payment terms. Put this in structured outputs so the decision memo can compare suppliers.

HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP should be modeled as: agents may send inquiries, negotiate within limits (max unit price, max sample spend, MOQ ceiling, payment-term floor) and request samples. Anything binding (placing an order, paying, signing an NDA) goes to the founder via email or SMS memo, and a 'proceed' reply triggers the Executor. This mirrors Accio's approval gate and Trade Assurance mechanics (a human clicks pay).

tools.name: AgentMail (core email API for agents)
tools.what_it_is: An email provider built for AI agents (YC S25). You create real inboxes through an API, send and reply in threads, receive mail through webhooks, WebSockets or polling webhooks, and get attachment text extracted for you. It has TS and Python SDKs, a CLI, and a hosted MCP server.
key_capabilities: Create inboxes over the API (POST /v0/inboxes) with username, domain, display_name, client_id for idempotency, and arbitrary metadata. Defaults to @agentmail.to; custom domains and subdomains are supported.
Messages: send, reply, reply-all and forward. Send takes labels, custom headers, cc/bcc, reply_to, attachments and track_opens. An Idempotency-Key header prevents duplicate sends.
Threads: list, search, get and update labels. A thread_id comes on every message.received event, which makes it the natural key for mapping one supplier conversation to one Naive session.
Reply extraction: extracted_text and extracted_html strip quoted history (Chinese 'wrote:' markers are explicitly supported) and boilerplate footers.
Attachment text extraction: Get Attachment returns download_url plus text_url for PDF (text layer only), DOC/DOCX and XLSX. Images, scanned PDFs, PPT and XLS are not extracted.

20 webhook event types: message.received, sent, delivered, bounced, complained, rejected, opened, plus .spam/.blocked/.unauthenticated variants. Delivery is at-least-once (dedupe on event_id), signed via Svix, and can be scoped per inbox or pod. Polling webhooks need no public URL.
WebSockets: a persistent subscribe-by-inbox stream that needs no public URL. The TS SDK reconnects automatically.
Drafts with labels, send_at scheduling, and scoped API-key permissions (draft_create without message_send) give a real approval gate.
Allow/block lists, auto-forwarding to verified addresses (added Nov 3 2026), Agent Armor prompt-injection scanning, IMAP/SMTP access, and a calendar per inbox.
tools.api_and_setup: Base URL https://api.agentmail.to/v0/ with Authorization: Bearer <key>; keys come from console.agentmail.to. SDKs: npm `agentmail` (v0.5.53, published 2026-11-06; `import { AgentMailClient } from "agentmail"`) and PyPI `agentmail` (v2.0.25). `agentmail-toolkit` (npm 0.18.0) wraps the API as Vercel AI SDK tools. The hosted MCP server is https://mcp.agentmail.to/mcp: OAuth for Claude and ChatGPT, header x-api-key for other clients, 47 tools; an `agentmail-mcp` stdio bridge exists on npm and PyPI. Pricing: Free is $0 with 3 inboxes, 100 emails/day (3k/mo), 3 GB, a 'Sent via AgentMail' footer, and Discord-only support. Developer is $20/mo (10 inboxes, 10k/mo, 1k/day, no footer). Startup is $200/mo (150 inboxes, 15k/day). Add-ons: $2/inbox, $2/domain, $5/seat. Early-stage startups can apply for one free month of the Startup tier at tally.so/r/QKrxj8. I found no hackathon-specific credit amount; organizers list AgentMail as a sponsor and say all participants get '$1k+ in credits'. Setup: sign up, create a key, create the inbox with the SDK, register a webhook on our Vercel/Render endpoint, done. Expect about 30-60 min for a basic send/receive loop.
tools.role_in_product: This is the procurement department's email layer. Each sourcing campaign (or each supplier) gets an inbox such as sourcing@ourco-procure.com. The agent emails RFQs (spec, MOQ, unit price, lead time, CE/FCC, samples) to supplier contact emails found on Alibaba, Made-in-China and supplier websites. Replies, PDF quotes and spec sheets come back through webhooks. The decision memo goes to the founder from the same system, and the founder's 'proceed' reply is caught by a webhook and resumes the right Naive session. On approval, the agent replies in-thread to the supplier to arrange samples and the shipping schedule.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: Email is the fallback and paper-trail channel next to WeChat and Alibaba messenger. Chinese factories that list on Alibaba and Made-in-China routinely accept English email RFQs and send quotations as PDF or XLSX attachments; AgentMail extracts the text so the agent can parse price tiers without OCR, as long as the PDF has a text layer. Reply extraction handles Chinese quoted history. Suppliers often answer an email with 'add my WeChat', so the email thread is where the WeChat ID gets captured and handed to the Mobilerun WeChat agent. The 16-hour time difference fits naturally: draft with send_at, or send Saturday evening SF time, and webhooks wake the right session overnight when Shenzhen replies. Store the thread_id -> naive_session_id mapping in Neon, or in inbox metadata if we use one inbox per supplier.
limitations_risks: Terms of service: AgentMail explicitly does not support cold outreach (ToS s.8(h)) and can suspend accounts that send unsolicited mail. Supplier RFQs to addresses published for inquiries are a grey area. Keep volume low (5-20 suppliers), personalize every message, add an opt-out line and an AI disclosure (s.4(f), 8(j)), and honor bounce and complaint events.

Deliverability into mainland China (QQ, 163/NetEase, Aliyun enterprise mail) is not documented anywhere. AgentMail inbound runs on Amazon SES, which has no China region, and offshore senders are throttled and filtered by QQ and NetEase. Expect some spam-folder placement. A new domain needs SPF, DKIM and DMARC; send plain text plus HTML with no links or images in the first email.

Inbound gotcha: supplier mail that passes no SPF/DKIM/DMARC is delivered with the 'unauthenticated' label and is not sent as message.received. You must also subscribe to message.received.unauthenticated, and the key needs label_unauthenticated_read. Mail that fails DMARC under quarantine or reject is dropped silently.

The free tier adds a 'Sent via AgentMail' footer and caps sending at 100/day. The custom-domain allowance conflicts between pages: pricing says 1, the rate-limits KB says none. Use the $20 Developer tier or the startup free month for a clean, branded sender.

Webhook payloads leave out the body when it exceeds 64 KiB, so call Get Message. Attachment URLs expire, so re-fetch rather than store them. Inline attachment requests are capped at 6 MB; URL-backed attachments go to about 30 MB.
An agent that signs itself up (agent sign-up API) gets only 1 inbox and 10 emails/day, and can send only to its own human until verified.

tools.name: AgentMail webhook to Naive session resume bridge (sub-feature / integration pattern)
tools.what_it_is: A glue pattern: AgentMail delivers each inbound supplier or founder email as a webhook (or over WebSocket) to our own endpoint on Vercel or Render. The endpoint looks up the waiting Naive session by AgentMail thread_id and resumes it with naive.sessions.send(), or answers a parked approval.
key_capabilities: Deterministic routing: AgentMail thread_id (and inbox_id) maps to a naive_session_id in Neon. A reply resumes the same long-running negotiation session with its full context, instead of starting a fresh session the way Naive's own inbound email does.
Naive sessions.send(sessionId, {message}) wakes an idle session into running, and every input is recorded on the event stream. Interrupts can be batched in with it.
Naive 'ask' policies park a tool call in pending_actions (stop_reason awaiting_approval) at storage cost only, for hours. A founder's 'proceed' email can be translated into the allow confirmation.
Naive outbound webhooks (session.idle, message.completed, budget.exceeded) tell our backend when to email the decision memo or update the dashboard.
AgentMail polling webhooks or WebSockets avoid exposing a public URL during local development.
tools.api_and_setup: 1) Deploy a /api/agentmail-webhook route on Vercel or Render and verify the Svix signature. 2) Call client.webhooks.create({ url, eventTypes: ['message.received','message.received.unauthenticated','message.bounced'] }). 3) Keep a Neon table threads(thread_id, inbox_id, supplier_id, naive_session_id, state). 4) In the handler, dedupe on event_id, fetch the full message if the body was omitted, then await naive.sessions.send(sessionId, { message: <fenced supplier reply + extracted attachment text> }). 5) Expose AgentMail to the Naive agent either through mcp_servers [{type:'url', name:'agentmail', url:'https://mcp.agentmail.to/mcp'}] with a vault static_bearer credential matched by URL, or as tools on our own app MCP endpoint that wrap the SDK and also write to Neon.
tools.role_in_product: This makes the procurement agent event-driven and autonomous overnight. Each supplier negotiation becomes a durable Naive session that sleeps cheaply and wakes exactly when that supplier replies. The founder's approval email resumes the coordinator session, which then executes the next steps.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: The same bridge should also carry WeChat and Alibaba messenger events from the Mobilerun phone agent: normalize every channel into the same threads table so one supplier session receives email and WeChat replies in order. Shenzhen replies that arrive between 1 and 9 am SF time wake sessions without a human, which is exactly what the judges score.
limitations_risks: AgentMail delivery is at-least-once, so the handler must be idempotent on event_id to avoid double-waking a session.

Naive caveat: once a chat has read people's data (mail, messages, connected apps), every send, every connected-app tool and every MCP tool asks for confirmation each time, even at 'allow'. Whether AgentMail MCP reads trigger this flag is unclear. If they do, autonomy breaks unless sends go through our own app MCP or backend. Test this early.

Naive MCP connector: the URL must be public HTTPS, tools default to 'ask' (set 'allow' per tool by name), each server contributes at most 100 tools, and secret headers cannot be set inline. Auth must come from the vault: static_bearer or mcp_oauth, and env_var is not available (501).
A running session must be interrupted before some operations. A send to a running session is queued as input.
verified_facts: Sending input to an idle Naive session wakes it into running; 'ask' policies park calls in pending_actions with stop_reason awaiting_approval, and a held tool consumes no budget while it waits: https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/session-operations.md
Naive outbound webhook events: session.idle, message.completed, budget.exceeded; signed envelope {id,type,created_at,data}; dedupe on id: https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/webhooks.md

Naive MCP connector: mcp_servers with type url; default permission ask; up to 20 servers; auth injected from the vault (static_bearer / mcp_oauth); inline secret headers rejected; at most 100 tools per server: https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/tools.md

tools.what_it_is: AgentMail's draft workflow combined with fine-grained API-key permissions. The agent can compose an email but cannot send it. A separate approver key or tool sends it after a human says yes.
key_capabilities: Drafts can be created with labels such as needs-approval and an optional send_at schedule.
API-key permissions can grant draft_create, draft_read and draft_update without message_send, message_reply or draft_send.
drafts.list(labels=[...]) across inboxes gives the approval queue for a dashboard.
Drafts with send_at can be queued for Shenzhen business hours (needs draft_send).
tools.api_and_setup: Create two keys in the console: an agent key with draft_* permissions only, and an approver key with draft_send. Our dashboard's 'Approve' button, or the founder's 'proceed' reply handled by the webhook bridge, calls drafts.send(inboxId, draftId, { removeLabels: ['needs-approval'] }) using the approver key.
tools.role_in_product: Enforces the hard authority limits outside the model. For example, any message that commits to a price, a PO or a sample payment above the limit has to become a draft for the founder. Routine RFQ and clarification emails go out under the agent key with send permission. This complements Naive's own 'ask' policies.

The same approval semantics should apply to WeChat messages sent by the phone agent (enforced in our backend).
limitations_risks: Only enforced if the agent's key truly lacks send permissions. Two keys means two vault credentials.
Naive already offers 'ask' policies and an Approvals primitive, so pick one approval surface to avoid double prompts.
