key_findings: Use AgentMail for supplier email, Naive Identity email (or AgentMail) for founder messages, Neon plus our own dashboard as the source of truth, and HubSpot only as an optional one-way mirror for the sponsor.

AgentMail's own docs say it 'does not support cold outreach' (ToS s.8(h)) and can suspend accounts. Supplier RFQs are a grey area: keep volume low (about 5-20 suppliers), personalize each message, include an opt-out line and an AI disclosure, and ideally confirm with support@agentmail.cc before the Saturday-evening send.

Two AgentMail gotchas for Chinese suppliers. First, deliverability to QQ, 163/NetEase and Aliyun mail is undocumented; offshore senders get throttled and filtered there. Second, inbound mail from supplier domains with no SPF/DKIM/DMARC is labeled 'unauthenticated' and is not sent as message.received, so you must also subscribe to message.received.unauthenticated (needs the label_unauthenticated_read permission). Mail that fails DMARC under quarantine or reject is dropped silently.

AgentMail fits the quote flow well. extracted_text strips quoted history, including Chinese 'wrote:' markers. text_url gives plain text from PDF (text layer only), DOCX and XLSX quotation attachments. Scanned or image quotes still need a vision model.

Naive's built-in Identity email starts a NEW session for each inbound email. It drops mail that fails authentication, caps waking at 5 messages/hr per sender, 20/hr per inbox and 10 thread turns/day, and asks before every email.send by default. For multi-turn supplier negotiations, route AgentMail webhooks into the existing session with naive.sessions.send(sessionId, {message}) using a thread_id -> session_id table in Neon.

Correction to the product context: Naive does have a human-in-the-loop primitive. 'ask' policies park tool calls as pending_actions (stop_reason awaiting_approval) at storage cost for hours, there is an Approvals primitive and an ask_operator tool, and outbound webhooks (session.idle) can trigger the founder decision-memo email.

Naive autonomy risk: once a chat has read people's data (mail, messages, connected apps), every send and every connected-app or MCP tool asks each time, even at 'allow'. This could stall the overnight autonomous loop if AgentMail or HubSpot are wired in as MCP tools. Test it early; the fallback is sending through our own backend or app MCP endpoint.

Wiring AgentMail into Naive: mcp_servers [{type:'url', name:'agentmail', url:'https://mcp.agentmail.to/mcp'}] plus a vault static_bearer credential. A live probe suggests the AgentMail MCP accepts Bearer auth. MCP tools default to 'ask', so set 'allow' per tool by name. Alternatively, wrap the `agentmail` npm SDK in our own tools.

AgentMail Drafts plus scoped API keys (agent key: draft_create only; approver key: draft_send) enforce the hard authority limits outside the model, and send_at schedules messages for Shenzhen business hours.

AgentMail pricing: Free gives 3 inboxes, 100/day, and a 'Sent via AgentMail' footer. Developer at $20/mo removes the footer. A free month of the Startup tier is available on application. I found no event-specific AgentMail credit amount; the hackathon says all participants get '$1k+ in credits'.

HubSpot changed recently: new legacy private apps cannot be created as of Oct 26 2026. Use Service Keys (Development > Keys > Service keys, Bearer pat-na1-..., REST only, no webhooks). Rate limits on Free are 100 requests per 10 s and 250k/day.

HubSpot Free reportedly allows 1 deal pipeline and 10 custom properties account-wide (third-party sources). A developer test account gets a 90-day Enterprise trial, which removes the caps. Communications API channel types are only WHATS_APP, LINKEDIN_MESSAGE and SMS, with no WeChat, so log WeChat touches as Notes.

The HubSpot remote MCP (GA Apr 2026) requires OAuth 2.1 PKCE, and Naive's vault mcp_oauth does not refresh tokens. Skip it and use REST with a Service Key from our backend, or the HubSpot Agent CLI for one-time pipeline setup.

Naive also has a built-in CRM (crm.read and crm.write, /v1/crm/contacts) with fixed sales stages (lead, talking, proposal, won, lost), available only when the company template declares it. It is a weaker fit than our own Neon schema for procurement stages.

key_findings: Apify's role is supplier discovery and enrichment, not outreach. I found no public Apify actor that sends Alibaba inquiries or WeChat messages. Several Alibaba actors say outright that they do not contact suppliers or log in, and the Alibaba scrapers return only a contactSupplierUrl (Alibaba's own inquiry form) with no phone, email or WeChat (https://apify.com/rel8ble/alibaba-supplier-search-scraper, https://apify.com/silentflow/alibaba-scraper). The actual WeChat or Alibaba-messenger send has to go through Mobilerun or Naive's built-in `mobile` and `browser` tools.

Best path from scraped data to WeChat: 1688 shops sometimes publish a mobile number. lentic_clockss/1688-global-scraper returns `phones` (type mobile), the Wangwang IM link, address and `org` company name (https://apify.com/lentic_clockss/1688-global-scraper). Chinese mobile numbers are usually searchable as WeChat 'add friend' IDs (inference, but standard practice in China), so a scraped phone becomes the handle the Mobilerun agent adds on WeChat. Alibaba.com hides all contact data, so on Alibaba the in-platform inquiry form or messenger is the only channel.

Naive can call MCP servers directly (verified at https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/tools.md). The agent config takes `mcp_servers: [{type:'url', name, url}]`, up to 20 servers, HTTPS and public URLs only. Auth comes from vault credentials (`static_bearer` or `mcp_oauth`) matched by URL; inline Authorization headers are rejected. MCP tools default to `ask` and must be set to `permission: 'allow'` per tool in `tools.configs` to run unattended. Apify MCP (https://mcp.apify.com, Bearer token) therefore fits the `static_bearer` path, and Monid MCP (https://mcp.monid.ai/v1, OAuth) would need `mcp_oauth`, which I have not tested.

Gotcha that hurts autonomy (verified, same Naive tools doc): once a chat has read people's data (contacts, mail, messages, a connected app), every send, `mobile`, `data_run`, `web_fetch` and every MCP tool asks for approval each time, even when set to `allow`, and `bash` is refused. Design implication: keep the scraping/research agent separate from the agent that reads supplier replies (email inbox or WeChat via `mobile`), and pass results through the Teams board or files.

Naive already has a human-approval primitive, despite the earlier assumption that it had none. A `permission: 'ask'` tool pauses the session (`requires_action`) until a person answers with a `tool.confirm` event (https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/tools.md). Setting the supplier-facing 'commit/proceed' send tool to `ask` gives the founder approval gate for free. Naive also lists a built-in `mobile` tool (cloud Android or iPhone: tap, type, launch_app), which is the natural WeChat sender.

Naive has its own Monid-like data catalogue: built-in `data_search` / `data_describe` / `data_run`, about 1,900 read-only endpoints from 51 sources in 18 domains, including `compliance` (KYB, sanctions, company registries), `trade` (customs shipment records), `shopping`, `people` and `companies`. Runs are capped at 25 results and 2 minutes, and the median price is about $0.0015 (https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/data.md). It looks very similar to Monid (1,608 endpoints from 54 providers, median $0.0015 per the notis.ai review), but no source confirms that Naive runs on Monid. Check `data_search` first: if it already has a supplier-risk or customs-trade tool, no extra integration is needed.

Apify integration recommendation: put a thin backend (Vercel or Render) in front of Apify. It calls `apify-client` (`client.actor(id).call(input)`, then `client.dataset(run.defaultDatasetId).listItems()`), normalizes the output from the Alibaba, 1688 and Made-in-China actors into one supplier schema, stores it in Neon, and exposes a single MCP tool `find_suppliers` to Naive. A Naive fullstack app can declare `mcp: '/mcp'` and the platform injects the auth (`VETTA_MCP_TOKEN`). This is more robust than handing the LLM 7,000 raw actors, because actor schemas differ wildly.

Apify costs for the demo are tiny. Examples: rel8ble Alibaba supplier search is $0.60 per 1,000 suppliers (50 suppliers = $0.03), lentic_clockss 1688 is $3 per 1,000 rows plus a $0.005 start fee, scrapesage Made-in-China starts at $1.10 per 1,000 products. The Free plan gives $5 a month with no card, 5 concurrent runs and $8/GB residential proxy (https://apify.com/pricing). Sync runs (`run-sync-get-dataset-items`) time out at 300 s with a 408 and accept `maxItems` and `maxTotalChargeUsd` caps (https://docs.apify.com/api/v2/act-run-sync-get-dataset-items-post).

Reliability risk: almost all China-marketplace actors are community-built with very few users and no ratings. rel8ble has 1 user, silentflow 7, lentic_clockss 10, xtracto 33; automation-lab 1688 has 155 users and a 3.0/5 rating; scrapesage Made-in-China has a 5.0 rating and 72 users. Plan on smoke-testing two actors per marketplace in the first hour and keeping a fallback. Field fill rates are partial (rel8ble: response time 12%, verified 62%).

Monid (https://monid.ai) is a pay-per-call tool gateway ('OpenRouter for agent tools'). It has REST at https://api.monid.ai (POST /v1/discover, /v1/inspect, /v1/run; GET /v1/runs/:id; Bearer `monid_live_...`), a remote MCP at https://mcp.monid.ai/v1 (OAuth), a CLI (`@monid-ai/cli`) and a SKILL.md. New accounts get $1 of free credit (MONID-SIGNUP). For our route the useful pieces are Saperly phone calls (about $0.26/min hosted, $1–2 per number; +86 support not confirmed), TikHub read-only WeChat endpoints (WeChat search, Official Account articles and profiles, about $0.01 per call), Apify actors without an Apify account (41 Apify endpoints) and AgentMail. Nothing in Monid sends WeChat or WhatsApp messages, and I found no translation endpoint (none is needed, since the LLM handles Chinese natively).

No Chinese freight-quote, currency or dedicated supplier-verification API was confirmed in either catalogue. Verification can be pieced together from: factline/alibaba-1688-supplier-risk-check (UFLPA, BIS Entity List, sanctions, USCC licence check, about $0.01 per supplier), Naive `compliance` and `trade` domains, WeChat Official Account lookup (zen-studio's actor claims to resolve the verified company behind an account), and Alibaba's own trust fields (Gold, Verified, Trade Assurance, verifiedBy SGS, years on Alibaba, response rate).

Timing: kick off Apify scraping and supplier ranking Saturday morning SF time and send first-contact messages Saturday afternoon or evening, so Shenzhen suppliers (about 16 h ahead) see them on Sunday morning their time. Apify runs finish in minutes, so scraping is not the bottleneck; WeChat friend-request acceptance is.

key_findings: Outbound phone calls are now a native OpenAI feature, but they run on GPT-Live, not the Realtime API. Create a call with POST /v1/live/sessions, model 'gpt-live-1', transport.type 'sip', an E.164 destination and your own SIP trunk (Twilio or Telnyx, sips: URL, TLS + SRTP). Call progress, transcript deltas and tool delegation come over a sideband WebSocket at wss://api.openai.com/v1/live/sessions/{id}/attach. Ringing is capped at 3 minutes and a connected call at 2 hours. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/voice-sip. Outbound became generally available on Nov 4, 2026, three days before the hackathon, so expect rough edges.

Calling China is expensive. Twilio's published outbound rate to China mobile numbers (+86 13x/15x/18x) is $0.3432/min and to landlines $0.3231/min (Twilio OutboundVoicePricing.csv, downloaded today). GPT-Live adds $0.05/min, plus backend model tokens. A 5-minute supplier call therefore costs roughly $2, versus about $0.35 for the same call to a US number.

The real Chinese-supplier channel is WeChat text and voice notes, plus Alibaba Trade Manager. Cold PSTN calls from a US number to Chinese mobiles are often ignored or flagged as spam (my inference, not verified). Voice calling is best positioned as a showpiece: an English-speaking Alibaba sales rep, or a teammate playing a Shenzhen supplier in Mandarin on stage. It should not be the main path.

Naive routing: Naive's docs never mention OpenRouter or BYOK. Every call goes through Naive's own 'model router' to an 'aggregated inference network' that 'asks the network for the fastest provider'. The example id z-ai/glm-5.3-flash exists verbatim in OpenRouter's public /api/v1/models list, but Naive also shows HuggingFace-style ids (zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8), so I could not confirm the backend. In practice, OpenRouter (sponsor) credits can't be spent through Naive agents unless the Naive team says otherwise. Use OpenRouter directly from tools or our own backend.

Naive's model proxy (api.vetta.sh/v1/proxy/openai/v1) rejects response_format, tool_choice and image inputs, and its catalogue lists no OpenAI ids in the examples. Vision (WeChat screenshots, spec sheets) and strict-JSON calls must therefore hit OpenAI or OpenRouter directly. Do this from a Naive Computer sandbox or a small backend tool, with the key stored in the Naive vault.

Naive has no telephony voice calls. Phone identity is US-only, at most 3 numbers per org, inbound SMS only, and outbound SMS returns 501. Naive's 'Voice $0.08/min' is a hands-free voice chat with the agent, capped at 10 minutes, not a phone call. Naive audio endpoints (STT/TTS/S2S) are batch only. This is a gap that OpenAI GPT-Live plus a Twilio trunk fills.

Recommended OpenAI models (Nov 2026 pricing, per 1M tokens in/out): gpt-6.1-sol at $2/$10 for negotiation and the decision memo, gpt-6-luna at $0.10/$0.50 for cheap image or text parsing, gpt-6-astra at $10/$50 for hard reasoning only, and gpt-realtime-2.1 for in-session tool-calling voice. gpt-live-1 is $0.05/min plus backend. gpt-realtime-translate is about $0.034/min and outputs 13 languages including Chinese. Transcription: gpt-transcribe at about $0.0045/min, gpt-4o-transcribe at about $0.006/min.

Chinese-native LLMs on OpenRouter are very cheap and good at Mandarin business register. Live list prices pulled from openrouter.ai/api/v1/models today (in/out per 1M): z-ai/glm-5.3-flash $0.034/$0.083; deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 $0.006/$0.50 (text and image); qwen/qwen3.8-flash $0.15/$0.47; qwen/qwen3.8-max-prime $4/$12; moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro $2/$10. All of these advertise structured_outputs support.

OpenAI vision docs warn that the model 'may not perform optimally' on non-Latin text such as Japanese or Korean. Chinese is not named but falls in the same category. For WeChat screenshots, use detail 'original' or 'high' on gpt-6.x/gpt-5.5 and crop or enlarge the chat region. Cross-check Chinese OCR with a Chinese VLM (qwen3.8-flash or glm-5.3-flash, both accepting images on OpenRouter).

Mandarin voice quality: one hands-on review rates GPT-Live Mandarin 4/5, versus 5/5 for Gemini Live and Doubao. Plain Mandarin is smooth, but mixing in English words (for example 'MOQ', 'CE', 'FCC') causes 1–2 s hesitations. There is no official Mandarin WER or language parameter for gpt-live-1. Script the call to say spec terms in Mandarin (起订量, 交期, 样品, CE认证).

Legal: open every call with an AI disclosure and a recording notice. California, where the founder is, requires all parties to consent to recording (known law, not fetched). The FCC treats AI voices as 'artificial' under the TCPA for US-bound calls. China's CAC AI-content labelling measures (effective Sep 1, 2025) push toward disclosing AI-generated voice. Chinese telemarketing rules cover consumers, while B2B supplier calls are lower risk. All China-law points come from secondary sources.

Timing: Shenzhen is 16 hours ahead, so 6–9pm Saturday in SF is 10am–1pm Sunday in Shenzhen. Many factory sales reps work Sundays via WeChat, but phone pickup on a Sunday is uncertain. Schedule voice calls as a fallback for suppliers who replied 'call me', and send WeChat or Alibaba text first.

Hackathon credits: the event lists OpenAI and OpenRouter as sponsors and promises '$1k+ in credits' for all participants, but I found no specific OpenAI or OpenRouter amounts. gpt-live-1 is not available on the OpenAI Free tier (the Build tier allows 50 concurrent sessions), so confirm the credited org is on a paid tier.

tools.name: OpenAI GPT-Live-1 outbound SIP voice calls (via Twilio or Telnyx SIP trunk)
tools.what_it_is: OpenAI's full-duplex speech-to-speech voice model (gpt-live-1). It can now place outbound phone calls over your own SIP trunk. The voice layer talks while a backend model (Responses delegation, e.g. gpt-6-luna or gpt-6.1-sol, or your own agent via client delegation) does reasoning and tool calls.
key_capabilities: Outbound calls: POST /v1/live/sessions with session.model 'gpt-live-1' and transport {type:'sip', destination:'+86...', trunk:{provider_url:'sips:...:5061', auth:{type:'digest',username,password}, caller_number:'+1...'}}

Sideband WebSocket wss://api.openai.com/v1/live/sessions/{id}/attach streams transport.ringing, transport.answered and transport.failed, plus session.input_transcript.delta and session.output_transcript.delta (with start_ms/end_ms) and delegation events

Delegation modes fixed per session: 'responses' (OpenAI runs the backend model with your tools) or 'client' (your own agent, e.g. a Naive session, answers the delegations). A native 'decisions' type also exists.
Two-way DTMF (transport.dtmf.send and .received) to get through phone menus, plus refer (transfer) and hangup endpoints
store:true keeps a stereo WAV (caller left, agent right) for 30 days at GET /v1/live/sessions/{id}/content. The text transcript has to be assembled from the deltas yourself.
Reported turn-taking latency of about 0.8 s versus 1.41 s for gpt-realtime-2.1 (community announcement thread). 12 voices.
tools.api_and_setup: OpenAI API key with server-side session creation. Endpoints: POST /v1/live/sessions, the WSS attach URL, and POST .../hangup and .../refer. Pricing: $0.05/min billed per second, plus backend model tokens. No Free-tier access; the Build tier allows 50 concurrent sessions. You need a SIP trunk that supports TLS signalling on 5061 and SDES-SRTP media, e.g. a Twilio Elastic SIP Trunk or Telnyx with digest credentials and a purchased number as caller ID. OpenAI media IPs: 13.79.45.80/28, 23.98.140.64/28, 40.67.149.176/28, 40.83.204.240/28. Carrier cost to China via Twilio is about $0.32–$0.34/min. Setup: buy a number, create a trunk with credentials and SRTP, enable China in geo permissions, create the session, attach the sideband, persist transcript deltas, then run a summary pass with gpt-6.1-sol and structured output.
tools.role_in_product: The 'phone the supplier' and 'phone the human candidate' channel for the sourcing department. A Naive 'Caller' agent receives a structured call brief (supplier, questions on MOQ, unit price, lead time, CE/FCC, samples, plus the hard negotiation limits). It invokes a tool that starts a GPT-Live session, waits for session.closed, and writes the transcript, WAV link and a structured summary to the Naive board or files. The coordinator then folds this into the founder's decision memo. With client delegation, the voice layer's 'what's my max price?' questions can be answered by our own policy service, which enforces authority limits deterministically.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: This is a secondary channel next to WeChat and Alibaba messaging. Use it when a supplier says 'call me' or lists a mobile number on Alibaba, or for English-speaking export sales reps. Instructions run in Mandarin ('您好，我是X公司的AI采购助理，本次通话会录音…'). The agent reads the spec terms in Chinese, asks MOQ, price tiers, lead time, certifications and sample cost, and never commits beyond limits ('I need to confirm with my founder'). Post-call, gpt-6.1-sol or Qwen produces a bilingual summary that goes into the memo. For the demo, the safest wow moment is a live call to a teammate's phone acting as a Shenzhen supplier in Mandarin, with transcript and memo appearing in the UI.
limitations_risks: Outbound GA was announced Nov 4, 2026, so it is very new. Community reports say the frontend sometimes says goodbye without delegating, so end-call tools don't fire. Add a server-side timeout and hangup.
The voice layer has no tools and no image input. Every action goes through delegation, which adds latency, and interrupting speech does not cancel backend work.
No documented language parameter. Mandarin is rated about 4/5 in a third-party review, and English terms mid-sentence cause 1–2 s hesitation.
China PSTN cost is about $0.34/min on Twilio. Chinese mobiles may screen or ignore overseas numbers, Sunday pickup is uncertain, and caller ID from a +1 number looks like spam.
Destination must be E.164 (no SIP URIs). The sideband replays only 3 s of events, so attach immediately or you lose transcript.
Legal: needs AI and recording disclosure. California requires all-party recording consent, the FCC/TCPA covers AI voice to US numbers, and China's AI-labelling rules apply.
Not available on the Free tier, so the hackathon credit org must be on a paid tier.
verified_facts: Outbound SIP calling is available to all organizations through the Live API (POST /v1/live/sessions, transport.type 'sip', E.164 destination, trunk.provider_url must be sips:, TLS + SDES-SRTP), not the Realtime call-creation endpoint. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/voice-sip

Ringing is limited to 3 minutes and a connected call to 2 hours, and neither is configurable. Sideband events: transport.ringing, transport.answered, transport.failed, DTMF events. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/voice-sip

gpt-live-1 costs $0.05 per minute of voice session, billed per second with no rounding up. Backend model and tool usage is billed separately. Concurrent sessions: Free not supported, Build 50, Launch 300, Grow 500. No image input, no structured outputs. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-live-1

Transcripts arrive via session.input_transcript.delta and session.output_transcript.delta. With store:true, a stereo WAV is downloadable for 30 days from GET /v1/live/sessions/{session_id}/content. session.closed reports usage.seconds and reason. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-conversations
Delegation is either 'responses' (e.g. model gpt-6-luna) or 'client', fixed at session creation. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-delegation
Twilio Programmable Outbound to China is $0.32310/min, and to China mobile $0.34320/min. Source: https://assets.cdn.prod.twilio.com/pricing-csv/OutboundVoicePricing.csv

GPT-Live outbound telephony GA was announced Nov 4, 2026, with Telnyx and Twilio as launch partners (secondary source). Source: https://cryptobriefing.com/gpt-live-outbound-telephony-api-general-availability/

Reported latency is 0.798 s turn-taking versus 1.41 s for GPT-Realtime-2.1, and the voice layer cannot take images (community announcement thread). Source: https://community.openai.com/t/introducing-gpt-live-1-in-the-api/1396471
unverified_or_inferred: Twilio Elastic SIP Trunking termination rates to China may differ from the Programmable Voice CSV rate. I couldn't retrieve a SIP-trunk-specific China rate, and Telnyx China rates were not checked.
That Chinese carriers or handsets often screen international calls as spam, and that suppliers prefer WeChat voice over PSTN, is inference.
Mandarin quality is based on one third-party review, and there is no official Mandarin benchmark for gpt-live-1.
Effort estimate assumes a Node backend deployed on Render or Vercel plus a Twilio account already verified for international calling.

tools.name: OpenAI Realtime API (gpt-realtime-2.1 / -mini) + Twilio Media Streams via OpenAI Agents SDK
tools.what_it_is: The older, tool-native speech-to-speech path. A RealtimeAgent/RealtimeSession from @openai/agents/realtime connects to a Twilio call through TwilioRealtimeTransportLayer from @openai/agents-extensions. Outbound calls are placed with Twilio's REST calls.create plus TwiML <Connect><Stream> to your WebSocket server. Native SIP on Realtime is inbound only (accept at /v1/realtime/calls/{id}/accept).
key_capabilities: Function calling and remote MCP inside the voice session, with no delegation hop
Agent handoffs and guardrails via the Agents SDK (TypeScript)
Image input supported on gpt-realtime-2/2.1 (unlike gpt-live-1)
Ready-made Twilio transport that handles audio format and interruptions
tools.api_and_setup: npm i @openai/agents @openai/agents-extensions twilio. You need a public WSS endpoint (Render web service or ngrok), a Twilio number, and X-Twilio-Signature validation on both webhook and WS upgrade. Pricing for gpt-realtime-2.1: audio $32 in / $0.40 cached / $64 out per 1M tokens, text $4/$24. gpt-realtime-2.1-mini: audio $10/$0.30/$20. Third-party estimates put it at roughly $0.05–$0.18/min for 2.1 depending on caching. Twilio Media Streams adds carrier minutes (China mobile $0.3432/min).
tools.role_in_product: A fallback if GPT-Live outbound misbehaves. Same Caller-agent tool interface, but the voice agent can directly call tools like get_negotiation_limits, log_quote and schedule_followup within the session.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: Same as the GPT-Live route (Mandarin supplier call, transcript, structured quote). Choose this path if you need in-call tool calls to be deterministic or you already know the Agents SDK.
limitations_risks: Outbound requires bridging Twilio Media Streams (extra server and latency) instead of native outbound SIP.
Older agents-js issues reported static or broken audio after multi-agent handoffs on the Twilio transport (#122, #168). Avoid handoffs mid-call.
gpt-realtime and gpt-realtime-mini retire Jan 20, 2027. Use gpt-realtime-2.1.
Community report: gpt-realtime-2.1-mini not calling function tools over SIP in some cases.
Higher turn-taking latency than GPT-Live (about 1.41 s reported).
verified_facts: gpt-realtime-2.1 costs audio $32.00 / $0.40 cached / $64.00, text $4.00 / $0.40 / $24.00, image input $5.00 per 1M tokens. gpt-realtime-2.1-mini costs audio $10/$0.30/$20. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing

Realtime SIP inbound: realtime.call.incoming webhook, POST /v1/realtime/calls/$CALL_ID/accept with model gpt-realtime-2.1, plus /reject, /refer and /hangup. Monitor via wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime?call_id=. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/voice-sip

TwilioRealtimeTransportLayer from @openai/agents-extensions bridges Twilio Media Streams to a RealtimeSession, and the server must validate X-Twilio-Signature. Source: https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/extensions/twilio/
Twilio China mobile outbound costs $0.3432/min. Source: https://assets.cdn.prod.twilio.com/pricing-csv/OutboundVoicePricing.csv
unverified_or_inferred: Per-minute cost ranges come from third-party blogs (forasoft, cekura), not OpenAI.
Whether the 2025 handoff audio bugs are fixed in current agents-js was not checked.

tools.name: OpenAI vision (Responses API input_image) for WeChat screenshots, Alibaba listings and spec sheets
tools.what_it_is: Image understanding in the Responses API on gpt-6.x, gpt-5.x and gpt-6-luna. It reads phone screenshots (WeChat chats operated via Mobilerun or the Naive mobile computer), product listing pages, PDF or image spec sheets and quotation tables, and returns schema-validated JSON.
key_capabilities: Images via URL, base64 data URL, or Files API file_id (purpose 'vision')
detail: low / high / original / auto. 'original' handles dense or computer-use screenshots on gpt-6-astra and gpt-5.5, where auto equals original.
Up to 1,500 images and 512 MB per request. Patch-based token cost (a 1024x1024 image is about 1,229 tokens on gpt-6-astra).
Combine with Structured Outputs (text.format json_schema, strict) to extract {supplier, MOQ, price tiers, lead_time, certs[], sample_cost, currency} from a WeChat screenshot or a quotation image.
tools.api_and_setup: npm i openai. Call client.responses.create({model:'gpt-6-luna' or 'gpt-6.1-sol', input:[{role:'user', content:[{type:'input_text',...},{type:'input_image', image_url:'data:image/png;base64,...', detail:'high'}]}], text:{format:{type:'json_schema', strict:true, schema}}}). Prices per 1M tokens: gpt-6-luna $0.10/$0.50, gpt-6.1-sol $2/$10, gpt-6-astra $10/$50. This can't go through Naive's model proxy, which rejects image inputs and response_format. Call OpenAI directly from a Naive Computer shell, a skill script, or our own backend tool, with the key kept in the Naive vault.
tools.role_in_product: The 'eyes' of the procurement agents. It parses every screenshot that the phone-operating agent (Mobilerun / Naive mobile) captures, turns unstructured supplier replies into rows in the supplier comparison table (Neon/Postgres), and reads certification images (CE/FCC certificates, test reports) to flag missing or suspicious certs for the decision memo.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: This is critical for the WeChat route, because WeChat has no API. The Mobilerun agent opens the chat and screenshots new messages. Vision extracts the Chinese text, quoted prices, voice-note transcriptions shown on screen, and images of product or packaging. The extraction becomes structured quote JSON plus a 'needs follow-up' list, and the agent drafts the next WeChat reply (in Chinese, via a Chinese LLM). It also reads Alibaba or 1688 product pages and supplier certification badges.
limitations_risks: OpenAI documents weaker performance on non-Latin text (cites Japanese and Korean, so Chinese is likely affected too). Crop or enlarge the chat bubbles, use detail 'original' or 'high', and cross-check with a Chinese VLM.
Small or rotated text and chart reading are listed weak spots.
Image tokens count toward TPM limits. Low detail isn't always cheaper on patch-based models.
Not routable through Naive's proxy, so it needs a separate API key and billing path.
verified_facts: input_image accepts a URL, base64 data URL or file_id. detail can be low, high, original or auto (auto behaves like original for gpt-6-astra and gpt-5.5). Limit is 1,500 images and 512 MB per request. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/images-vision
Docs: 'The model may not perform optimally when handling images with text of non-Latin alphabets, such as Japanese or Korean.' Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/images-vision
gpt-6-luna costs $0.10 / $0.01 cached / $0.50, gpt-6.1-sol $2.00/$0.10/$10.00, and gpt-6-astra $10/$1/$50 per 1M tokens. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing
Naive OpenAI-door proxy refuses response_format and tool_choice, and the Anthropic door supports only text, tool_use and tool_result blocks. Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/proxy.md
Naive's model router also says image inputs are rejected on the proxy. Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router.md
unverified_or_inferred: Chinese OCR accuracy on WeChat screenshots was not benchmarked. I recommend a quick A/B against qwen/qwen3.8-flash.
Whether Naive's native agent harness (as opposed to the proxy) can pass screenshots to vision models was not verified.

tools.name: OpenAI Responses API + Structured Outputs for negotiation reasoning and the founder decision memo
tools.what_it_is: OpenAI's primary text and agent API (Responses), with strict JSON-schema outputs and hosted tools such as web_search. Use it for the high-stakes reasoning steps: negotiation strategy within authority limits, supplier scoring, and the final decision memo.
key_capabilities: text.format {type:'json_schema', strict:true} for guaranteed-shape quote, offer and memo objects
reasoning_effort control. gpt-6.1-sol ($2/$10) is a good balance, and gpt-6-astra ($10/$50) is for hard calls.
Batch and Flex at about 50% off for overnight bulk parsing of supplier replies
Also the backend for GPT-Live Responses delegation, so the same tools and prompts are reused on calls
tools.api_and_setup: npm i openai, OPENAI_API_KEY, client.responses.create. Pricing per OpenAI's page. gpt-5.6-sol has promo pricing until Nov 30, 2026. Hackathon OpenAI credit amount is unknown; check kickoff and Discord. Inside Naive, agents can use Naive's own structured-outputs capability. Direct OpenAI calls give strict schemas that Naive's proxy refuses.
tools.role_in_product: Negotiator and memo-writer. A deterministic policy layer holds the hard limits (max unit price, max MOQ, max sample spend). The model proposes counter-offers and a policy check rejects any out-of-bounds offer before sending. It produces a structured decision memo (ranked suppliers, landed-cost estimate, risks, recommendation, and 'Reply PROCEED to approve') that is emailed to the founder via AgentMail or shown in the UI.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: It turns the parsed WeChat, Alibaba or call data into the next message intent ('counter at $4.20 for 1k units, ask for CE test report and 2 samples via DHL'). A Chinese LLM then renders the intent in natural Mandarin business tone. On 'proceed', it generates the sample PO and shipping schedule message.
limitations_risks: A separate billing path from Naive's budgets, so token spend is outside Naive's micro-USD caps unless metered yourself.
Model ids (gpt-6.x 'astra', 'sol', 'terra', 'luna') are new. Pin ids and check availability on the credited org.
verified_facts: gpt-6-astra costs $10/$1/$50, gpt-6.1-sol $2/$0.10/$10, gpt-6.1-terra $1/$0.05/$5 and gpt-6-luna $0.10/$0.01/$0.50 per 1M tokens. Batch and Flex are about half price, and the gpt-5.6-sol promo runs until Nov 30, 2026. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing
Naive's proxy refuses response_format. Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/proxy.md
unverified_or_inferred: Model recommendations (sol for negotiation, luna for parsing) are my judgement, not benchmarked for this task.

tools.name: OpenAI speech: gpt-realtime-translate, gpt-transcribe and gpt-4o-transcribe (WeChat voice notes, live interpretation)
tools.what_it_is: Covers streaming speech translation at /v1/realtime/translations (70+ input languages to 13 outputs, including Chinese and English) and batch or streaming transcription models.
key_capabilities: gpt-realtime-translate auto-detects the source language and outputs translated speech plus text. Chinese works both as input and output.
Transcription: gpt-transcribe (about $0.0045/min), gpt-4o-transcribe (about $0.006/min), gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize, gpt-live-transcribe (about $0.017/min)
Translate costs about $0.034/min
tools.api_and_setup: Same OpenAI key. Translation is a Realtime session at /v1/realtime/translations with a target language. Transcription uses /v1/audio/transcriptions with a file upload. Alternatively, Naive's own POST /v1/media/audio/transcriptions (stt/auto) is billed inside Naive. It has no Mandarin guarantee, and its default STT is google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite.
tools.role_in_product: Turns supplier voice messages and call recordings into bilingual text for the memo. Lets the human founder optionally listen in on a supplier call with live English interpretation (a human-in-the-loop demo moment).
tools.role_in_supplier_route: Chinese suppliers frequently reply on WeChat with voice notes (语音). If the phone agent can export or forward the audio, transcribe it. Otherwise use WeChat's built-in 'Convert to Text' on-device and read the screen with vision. Translate gives a 'founder hears the Shenzhen supplier in English live' demo.
limitations_risks: Extracting audio files from WeChat on a cloud phone is hard. On-screen voice-to-text plus vision is likely simpler (inference).
Translate outputs only 13 languages and is translation-only, not an agent.
Unclear whether 'Chinese' output means Mandarin only.
verified_facts: Transcription per-minute estimates: gpt-realtime-translate $0.034, gpt-live-transcribe $0.017, gpt-transcribe $0.0045, gpt-4o-transcribe $0.006, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe $0.003. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing

gpt-realtime-translate has endpoint /v1/realtime/translations, 70+ input languages and 13 output languages including Chinese. Source: https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/voice_solutions/realtime_translation_guide

Naive audio: STT at /v1/media/audio/transcriptions (default google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite), TTS defaulting to openai/gpt-audio-mini or kokoro (English only). No realtime or streaming. Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/audio.md
unverified_or_inferred: The 70+/13 language counts come via the cookbook and search summary. I did not read the full cookbook page.

tools.name: OpenRouter model routing (OpenAI-compatible gateway, provider routing, fallbacks, BYOK, Auto Router)
tools.what_it_is: A unified OpenAI-compatible API (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, Chat Completions and Responses) to about 460 models across providers, with per-request routing controls, model fallbacks, structured outputs, BYOK and an auto-router.
key_capabilities: provider object: order, allow_fallbacks, require_parameters, data_collection:'deny', zdr, only/ignore, quantizations, sort ('price'|'throughput'|'latency'), preferred_max_latency, max_price
Model suffixes: ':nitro' (fastest, includes priority tiers) and ':floor' (cheapest, includes flex)
models:[...] fallback array, e.g. try qwen/qwen3.8-max-prime then deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
Structured outputs via response_format json_schema (or text.format on Responses). Filter models with ?supported_parameters=structured_outputs and set require_parameters:true.
openrouter/auto Auto Router (plugin auto-router with cost_tier) with no extra fee
BYOK: first $25,000/month of list-price inference has no fee, then 5%. Credit purchases carry a 5.5% platform fee (Standard). No markup on inference. No plan rate limits on paid models.
tools.api_and_setup: Create an API key at openrouter.ai and buy credits (sponsor credits if provided). Use npm i openai with baseURL 'https://openrouter.ai/api/v1', or the OpenRouter SDK. Optional headers HTTP-Referer and X-Title for attribution. Free models are capped at 20 req/min and 50/day, or 1,000/day after a $10 purchase. Setup takes about 15 minutes.
tools.role_in_product: One model bus for all non-Naive LLM calls: cheap Chinese models for drafting and parsing, OpenAI or Anthropic for the memo, and automatic fallback if a provider is down mid-demo. Use data_collection:'deny' or zdr for supplier PII. It is also the clean way to spend OpenRouter sponsor credits, since Naive doesn't document OpenRouter or BYOK.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: Route Chinese-language work (drafting WeChat messages in idiomatic business Mandarin, parsing 1688 listings, translating replies) to Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek or Kimi at a fraction of GPT cost. Use sort:'latency' or ':nitro' when a live chat exchange needs fast replies, and ':floor' or batch variants for overnight bulk parsing while Shenzhen is awake.
limitations_risks: Naive does not document OpenRouter, so we can't point Naive agents' own model at OpenRouter credits. OpenRouter is used only from tools, skills or the backend.
Per-provider differences (quantization, tool-calling quality) on open-weight models. Pin providers with order/only for the demo.
Listed prices change often (several changed Nov 4) and may show the cheapest endpoint, not the one that serves you.
Chinese-hosted providers (e.g. Alibaba, Z.ai, DeepSeek first-party) raise data-residency questions. Use ignore/zdr if needed.
verified_facts: BYOK has no fee on the first $25,000/month of list-price inference, then 5%. Credit purchase fee is 5.5% (Standard). No markup on inference and no plan rate limits on paid models. Free models are limited to 20 rpm and 50/day (1,000/day after $10 in credits). Source: https://openrouter.ai/pricing

BYOK is configured at /settings/integrations or via POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/byok, and supports OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, Fireworks and others. Source: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/auth/byok

Provider object fields (order, allow_fallbacks, require_parameters, data_collection, zdr, only, ignore, quantizations, sort, max_price) and the :nitro/:floor shortcuts. Source: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection
Structured outputs use response_format json_schema, or text.format on the Responses API. Source: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/structured-outputs
openrouter/auto Auto Router with auto-router plugin settings (cost_tier, allowed_models, excluded_models) and no extra fee. Source: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/routers/auto-router
The public model list at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models returned 461 models today, including z-ai/glm-5.3-flash. Source: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models
unverified_or_inferred: The OpenRouter sponsor credit amount for this hackathon is unknown.
Whether openrouter/auto restricts itself to structured-output-capable models is undocumented.

tools.name: Chinese-capable LLMs (Qwen 3.8, DeepSeek V4.1, GLM-5.3, Kimi K3.1) via OpenRouter, and Naive's relation to them
tools.what_it_is: Chinese-lab models with native Mandarin fluency and Chinese-commerce familiarity (1688/Alibaba terminology, 起订量, 含税价, FOB/EXW), available through OpenRouter. GLM is also the default in Naive's examples.
key_capabilities: z-ai/glm-5.3-flash at $0.034/$0.083 per 1M, 1M context, text, image and video input, structured outputs. This is the exact id used in Naive's quickstart.
deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 at $0.006/$0.50, 1M context, text and image, structured outputs. #1 by OpenRouter token share (third-party report).
qwen/qwen3.8-flash at $0.15/$0.47 (text, image, video). qwen/qwen3.8-max-prime at $4/$12 for top-quality Mandarin negotiation drafting. qwen/qwen3.8-omni-flash also takes audio input.
moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro at $2/$10, 1M context, text, image and video, structured outputs
Batch variants (:batch) are about 50% cheaper for overnight parsing
tools.api_and_setup: Through OpenRouter (same key and baseURL). Inside Naive, set the agent model to a catalogue id (e.g. 'z-ai/glm-5.3-flash' or 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731'), billed by Naive's router. Discover what Naive offers with GET /v1/models?search=qwen (auth required). The Naive catalogue is 'read live from the inference network' and filtered to tool-calling models with published prices. Naive's priority and loose windows give cheaper open-weight tariffs.
tools.role_in_product: Default 'worker' models: cheap, Chinese-fluent parsing, translation and drafting agents in the Naive team (e.g. a Sourcer agent scanning Alibaba or Made-in-China via Apify output, and a Messenger agent writing WeChat or Alibaba messages). Keep GPT-6.1-sol or similar only for the negotiator and memo, giving a large cost reduction overall.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: Writes natural, polite Chinese B2B messages ('您好！我们是美国一家做老人跌倒检测设备的初创公司…请问这款毫米波雷达模组的起订量、阶梯价、交期和CE/FCC认证情况？'). It interprets supplier slang and abbreviations, converts RMB to USD quotes including tax (含税/不含税) and shipping terms, and flags red flags such as a trading company versus a factory. A Chinese VLM (glm-5.3-flash or qwen3.8-flash) gives a second-opinion OCR of WeChat screenshots.

Naive has no BYOK, so OpenRouter sponsor credits can't pay for Naive-agent tokens.

Some list prices look anomalous (e.g. glm-5.2 $0.006 in / $6.8 out, kimi-k3 $0.192/$16), probably min-endpoint artifacts. Verify per-endpoint before relying on them.

key_findings: One correction to the product context: Naive DOES have a documented human-in-the-loop primitive. A tool set to permission 'ask' stops the session with stop_reason 'awaiting_approval' and lists the waiting call in pending_actions[]. You resolve it with `naive session confirm --allow/--deny` or `naive.sessions.confirmTool()`. The approver is recorded, and a held tool costs no budget while it waits, so it can wait for hours. MCP tools default to 'ask'. There is also a Reviews API. This is the 'proceed?' gate for the founder; no sponsor tool is needed to build it. (https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/policies.md, https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/session-operations.md, https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/tools.md)

Naive accepts up to 20 MCP servers per agent (`mcp_servers: [{type:'url', name, url}]`, public HTTPS only). Auth must come from Naive vault credentials (`static_bearer` or `mcp_oauth`); inline Authorization headers are rejected. So Neon MCP (https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp) and Stripe MCP (https://mcp.stripe.com, with an agent API key) can plug straight into Naive agents, each tool gated allow/ask/deny. (https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/tools.md)

Naive overlaps heavily with Vercel + Neon. It hosts 'fullstack' apps that come with a managed Postgres (db_query/db_rest/db_migrate) and their own MCP endpoint. It also receives inbound email and SMS through its own webhooks, which wake the agent, and has a built-in `mobile` tool for a cloud Android phone or iPhone. Use Vercel and Neon on purpose: for the sponsor prizes and the Best Design track, and for a better dashboard than Naive's. Do not use them because Naive lacks the capability. (https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/apps.md, https://usenaive.ai/docs/capabilities/webhooks.md)

Naive's own agent payment surfaces are switched off on the hosted service. Card issuing (prepaid $1-$150 virtual cards) answers 501 feature_not_configured, and the USDC-on-Base wallet is 'Phase 5 / not available yet'. Stripe is the only sponsor that could add agent spending, but Issuing for agents is itself in private preview. In practice, the demo should show 'budget authority' in our own Neon tables and through Naive approvals, not real money moving. (https://usenaive.ai/docs/identity/cards.md, https://usenaive.ai/docs/identity/wallet.md, https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/agents)

Stripe cannot realistically pay a Chinese supplier during the hackathon. Global Payouts lists China (CN) only under 'private preview currencies: CNY, USD', paid by wire, and access must be requested. The realistic path is Alibaba.com Trade Assurance: card (about 2.95% fee, reportedly a $12k per-transaction limit), T/T, PayPal, Pay Later. Guides recommend paying for samples by card through Trade Assurance. Our agent should send the founder a Trade Assurance order link and payment instructions for approval, not try to move money itself. (https://docs.stripe.com/global-payouts/recipient-countries, https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia/2026-04-22/cross-border-payouts-new-countries, https://seller.alibaba.com/blogs/2026/southeast-asia/b2b-trade/trade-assurance-complete-guide-alibaba-secure-payment)

Stripe's old Agent Toolkit npm packages (@stripe/agent-toolkit, @stripe/mcp, @stripe/ai-sdk) are deprecated and get no security fixes. The replacement is the hosted Stripe MCP at https://mcp.stripe.com. It has generic stripe_api_read/stripe_api_write tools and Treasury tools: send_money, transfer_money and convert_currency carry a 'Human confirmation' badge. Starting December 2026 it accepts only OAuth or 'agent API keys'; plain secret and restricted keys stop working after November 30, 2026. (https://github.com/stripe/agent-toolkit, https://docs.stripe.com/mcp)

Vercel Workflow (npm `workflow`, GA since April 2026) is a good fit for waiting on suppliers. `sleep()` can wait minutes to months without using compute, `createHook`/`createWebhook` pause a run until an external event arrives, and Hobby includes 50k events per month. Limits: Hobby functions max out at 300s, Hobby cron runs at most once per day (with jitter inside the hour), and Daemons cannot accept inbound connections. A Twilio media-stream WebSocket server therefore belongs on Render or another host, not Vercel. (https://vercel.com/kb/guide/background-workers-on-vercel, https://workflow-sdk.dev/docs/foundations/hooks, https://vercel.com/docs/cron-jobs/manage-cron-jobs)

Neon's free plan is enough for the hackathon: 100 projects, 100 CU-hours per project per month, 1 GB storage per project, 10 branches, no credit card, scale-to-zero after 5 minutes. The hosted MCP (https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp) has run_sql, run_sql_transaction and create_branch, and a read-only mode via ?readonly=true. Render free web services support WebSockets but sleep after 15 minutes idle and take about a minute to wake. That would break an incoming Twilio voice call, so pay for a $7/month Starter instance during the demo window. Background workers and cron jobs have no free tier ($7/month and up). Workspace plans have been flat since April 23, 2026 (Hobby $0, Pro $25). Render Workflows tasks run up to 24 hours, billed on Flex at $0.20 per active CPU-hour, with no free allowance. (https://render.com/docs/free, https://render.com/blog/upcoming-changes-to-workflows-pricing)

Luxor is not a fit. Its AI compute is reserved multi-year GPU capacity (B300/H200/H100 nodes), sales-led with no published self-serve price, and no hackathon credits turned up in my searches. Its developer cloud, Tenki, offers per-second Linux sandbox VMs, but Naive already provides a Computer sandbox. Self-hosting a Chinese LLM or a voice model is not worth it in 22 hours when OpenRouter (Qwen/DeepSeek) and OpenAI Realtime exist. Recommend skip. (https://luxor.tech/ai/compute, https://tenki.cloud/)

Timezone plan: Shenzhen is 16 hours ahead. Neither Vercel Hobby cron (daily only) nor Render is needed for the overnight follow-up loop. Use Naive deployments (cron) or a Vercel Workflow `sleep` until supplier business hours (about 09:00-18:00 Asia/Shanghai, which is 17:00-02:00 PST), then nudge suppliers who have not replied. Store every inbound reply in Neon with an external_id for idempotency so duplicate webhook deliveries are harmless.

Recommended infra stack for 22 hours: Naive as the agent runtime and approvals. Neon as the single source of truth, connected through MCP for agents and @neondatabase/serverless for the dashboard. Vercel for the Next.js dashboard, webhook receivers (AgentMail, Mobilerun, Stripe) and optional Workflow follow-ups. AI SDK v7 for the streaming decision-memo UI. Render only if we build the Twilio voice agent. Stripe for billing our own customers (Payment Link plus a Billing meter), with Stripe Issuing in sandbox as an optional 'sample-fee card' story. Skip Luxor.

tools.what_it_is: Frontend cloud for Next.js. It runs Fluid compute Functions, Vercel Workflow (durable 'use workflow' / 'use step' functions, GA April 2026), Queues (public beta), Daemons (always-on containers, beta), Cron, v0 (UI generation) and the Marketplace (Neon).

Workflow SDK (npm `workflow` v5.4.0): sleep() for minutes to months without compute; createHook()/createWebhook() pause until an external event; automatic step retries (3); FatalError; 10k steps per run; Hobby includes 50k events per month
createWebhook() exposes a public URL /.well-known/workflow/v1/webhook/:token; createHook() plus resumeHook() from your own authenticated route for approvals

tools.api_and_setup: `npx create-next-app` or a v0-generated app, then `vercel deploy`. Add Neon from the Marketplace to get the DATABASE_URL env var. Add webhook routes app/api/webhooks/{agentmail,mobilerun,stripe,naive}/route.ts, verifying signatures (Naive uses an HMAC-SHA256 `Vetta-Signature: v1=` header over `{timestamp}.{raw_body}` with a 300s replay window). Optional: `npm i workflow` and wrap the follow-up / approval flow in 'use workflow'. Hobby is free but limited to non-commercial use; Pro is $20 per user per month. Setup about 1 hour; dashboard 4-6 hours with v0.
tools.role_in_product: Hosts the founder-facing 'Procurement Department' dashboard: supplier pipeline, live conversation threads with translations, an offer comparison table, the decision memo, and a big Approve / Reject button. The button calls naive.sessions.confirmTool() on the pending 'ask' tool call, so the approval goes through Naive's own primitive. Vercel is also the public HTTPS ingress for third-party callbacks (AgentMail inbound email, Mobilerun task-finished callbacks, Stripe events, Naive outbound webhooks such as session idle / awaiting approval). Each callback writes to Neon and, where needed, sends a message into the relevant Naive session to wake the agent. Strong for the Best Design track.
tools.role_in_supplier_route: WeChat has no official inbound webhook for personal accounts, so new supplier messages arrive in one of three ways: (a) the phone agent polls the WeChat app on a cloud phone (Naive mobile or Mobilerun) and reports back, (b) Mobilerun callbacks hit a Vercel route, or (c) AgentMail or Alibaba email notifications hit a Vercel route. In every case the Vercel handler acks fast (well under 300s), upserts into Neon, and wakes the negotiator. A Vercel Workflow per supplier conversation can `sleep` until the next Shenzhen business window (about 09:00 Asia/Shanghai = 17:00 PST) and send follow-ups, using `Promise.race([hook, sleep('12h')])` to escalate suppliers who never reply. Hobby cron (daily only) is too coarse for this; use Workflow sleep or Naive deployments (cron).
